News.title: Royal fans convinced they’ve worked out Princess Eugenie’s baby name in major Instagram clue
News.content:
PRINCESS Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank announced the birth of their daughter yesterday – and royal fans think they’ve worked out her name.

The royal couple took to Instagram to share the news they had welcomed their third child but did not confirm what they’ve called her.



In a statement posted alongside a sweet snapshot of the newborn, Eugenie and Jack said: “Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

“We are beyond in love with our girlie,” they added.



While details of the baby girl’s name were not included in the upload, royal fans think the late Queen Elizabeth II‘s great-granddaughter and her husband may have added a hint.

Using Instagram’s music feature to add a backing track to the upload, Eugenie announced her daughter’s birth to the sound of Isn’t She Lovely by Stevie Wonder.

The iconic 1976 track was written by the music legend to celebrate the birth of his daughter, Aisha Morris.

Royal supporters have pointed out that Princess Eugenie and Jack may have used Aisha in their little girl’s full moniker and used the musical tribute to share a subtle hint at her name.

No details regarding the baby’s name were shared in the Royal Family’s official statement announcing her birth, either.

The announcement did, however, confirm that Princess Eugenie gave birth in the Portuguese capital of Lisbon and revealed the baby’s weight.



“Her Royal Highness Princess Eugenie and Mr Jack Brooksbank are delighted to announce the safe arrival of their daughter, born on Monday, 3rd August 2026, at 6.20pm, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal,” Buckingham Palace’s statement said.

“The baby was born weighing 6 pounds 9 ounces.

“Their Majesties The King and Queen and other members of The Royal Family were delighted to be informed of the news,” the announcement added.

Princess Eugenie and Jack are also parents to two sons – August Philip Hawke Brooksbank, born in 2021, and Ernest George Ronnie Brooksbank, born in 2023.

The names of both boys include sweet nods to Eugenie’s royal relatives, with August’s middle name paying tribute to the late Prince Philip and Ernest’s middle name given in honour of King George VI.



Eugenie and Jack’s daughter’s middle name will no doubt be given in honour of her great grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II.

It seems to have become tradition for the Queen’s grandchildren to give at least one of their daughters the middle name.

This includes Princess Beatrice, whose daughters are called Sienna Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi and Athena Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi.

Prince William’s daughter, Princess Charlotte, was also given the middle name, with a full moniker of Charlotte Elizabeth Diana.

Peter Phillips’ second-born daughter is Isla Elizabeth Phillips, while Zara Tindall’s second-born daughter is Lena Elizabeth Tindall.

And, of course, Prince Harry’s daughter, Princess Lilibet, was famously named using the nickname that Queen Elizabeth II used throughout her life.

News.title: Woman sexually assaulted on Tube during rush hour as cops release CCTV in hunt for man
News.content:
ATTACK PROBE Woman sexually assaulted on Tube during rush hour as cops release CCTV in hunt for man

COPS have released CCTV of a man they would like to speak to after a woman was allegedly sexually assaulted at a train station.

The alleged incident took place at around 5pm on June 15 at Bond Street Underground station, said British Transport Police.



A female passenger was reportedly sexually assaulted as she walked through the tunnel from the Elizabeth Line to the Central Line platform.

Cops launched an investigation and released a CCTV image of a man who they believe can help in connection with the incident.



Detectives would like to speak to the man pictured, as he may have information that could assist their investigation.

Anyone who recognises him is asked to text BTP on 61016 or call 0800 40 50 40, quoting reference 484 of 15 June.



Information can be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Security alert as ‘bomb drone’ crashes at German airport near Ukrainian plane & landing jet suffers mid-air collision
News.content:
A SUSPECTED bomb-fitted drone has crashed at a German airport near a Ukrainian plane, sparking a major security alert.

The unmanned vehicle was found as a DHL cargo plane struck a mystery object while climbing away from Leipzig/Halle airport overnight.



Police deployed a bomb disposal robot to inspect the stricken drone, which was found near a Ukrainian Antonov cargo plane shortly before midnight.

The airline has used Leipzig/Halle as an operating base since Russia‘s full-scale invasion in 2022.



The airport’s southern runway, a major hub for DHL and Antonov, remained closed while bomb experts examined the device.

X-ray imaging showed the drone was attached to a defective detonator.

The explosive may have been one that can be made easily from fertiliser and gasoline, according to Bild.

Several planes, including a passenger flight, were diverted overnight.

While air traffic was being redirected, one cargo plane had to abort its landing.

It then reportedly hit an unknown object before landing in Hanover, where minor damage to the nose section was discovered.



German airports have been on high alert after a string of unauthorised drone overflights have been spotted.

They have been seen worryingly near to military facilities, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies.

Police said that these overflights may be connected to Russian agents.



European security agencies have been probing a series of incendiary devices concealed in parcels that caught fire in 2024.

These incidents raised concerns that malicious actors may be planning to sabotage air cargo operators.

Putin was even suspected of planting a parcel bomb on a flight headed to a depot in the UK.

Some of the devices were found at a DHL warehouse in Leipzig and in freight shipments in transit across Europe.

The Leipzig device started burning as it was being loaded onto a plane after it had come from Lithuania.



The head of the German domestic intelligence agency said if it had exploded on the plane it could have brought it down.

An Interior Ministry spokesperson said they could determine no connection to these incidents with Tuesday night’s drone.

Russia has denied any involvement in the 2024 incidents and the more recent overflights.

DHL Group CEO Tobias Meyer said the German logistics firm was still investigating the incident while trying to minimise the effect on customers.

News.title: Serial killer nurse Lucy Letby will face NO new criminal charges as families of six more babies lose bid after review
News.content:
SERIAL killer nurse Lucy Letby will face no further criminal charges after the families of six more babies failed in a bid to overturn a decision not to prosecute her again.

Letby, 35, is serving 15 whole-life orders for murdering seven babies in a year-long reign of terror.



The nurse also tried to kill seven others at the Countess of Chester Hospital between June 2015 and June 2016 – but her case is at the centre of a high-profile miscarriage of justice campaign.

The latest allegations are related to six more infant collapses at the hospital and Liverpool Women’s Hospital, where the former neonatal nurse was previously employed.



In November 2024, the Crown Prosecution Service disclosed that it was considering further charges against the 36-year-old, who is currently serving a whole-life order.

But the CPS ruled in January that no new charges would be brought over potential offences of attempted murder and murder involving nine children, including two who died, because the evidential test was not met.

Six families subsequently requested an official review of the decisions concerning their children under the Victims’ Right to Review scheme.

However, an extensive review by an independent prosecutor has now upheld the original decision to bring no further charges against the former nurse.



Malcolm McHaffie, head of the CPS’s special crime division said: “In January 2026, after reviewing a file of evidence from Cheshire Constabulary, we decided that no further criminal charges should be brought against Lucy Letby, 36, relating to deaths and non-fatal collapses of babies at the Countess of Chester Hospital and Liverpool Women’s Hospital.

“The Crown Prosecution Service subsequently received requests in relation to six infants for the decisions to be reviewed under the Victims’ Right to Review (VRR) scheme.

“An extensive review of the case by a prosecutor independent of the original decisions, involving a re-examination of substantial evidence and material, has now been completed.

“Six offences of attempted murder were reconsidered in relation to six babies, but the review upheld the original decision not to bring any further criminal charges.

“The Crown Prosecution Service has written to the families involved and will offer meetings to answer any further questions.



“Our thoughts remain with them.”

Letby is serving 15 whole-life orders, following two trials in 2023 and 2024.

However, since her sentencing, there’s been growing feeling amongst many experts that her convictions were “unsafe”, and she could have been the victim of a miscarriage of justice.

The charges Letby has been convicted of in full Child A, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby injected air intravenously into the bloodstream of the baby boy. COUNT 1 GUILTY. Child B, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby attempted to murder the baby girl, the twin sister of Child A, by injecting air into her bloodstream. COUNT 2 GUILTY. Child C, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said Letby forced air down a feeding tube and into the stomach of the baby boy. COUNT 3 GUILTY. Child D, allegation of murder. The Crown said air was injected intravenously into the baby girl. COUNT 4 GUILTY. Child E, allegation of murder. The Crown said Letby murdered the twin baby boy with an injection of air into the bloodstream and also deliberately caused bleeding to the infant. COUNT 5 GUILTY. Child F, allegation of attempted murder. Letby was said by prosecutors to have poisoned the twin brother of Child E with insulin. COUNT 6 GUILTY. Child I, allegation of murder. The prosecution said Letby killed the baby girl at the fourth attempt and had given her air and overfed her with milk. COUNT 12 GUILTY. Child K, allegation of attempted murder. The prosecution said Letby compromised the baby girl as she deliberately dislodged a breathing tube. COUNT 14 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT AT ORIGINAL TRIAL, NOW GUILTY AFTER RETRIAL Child L, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said the nurse poisoned the twin baby boy with insulin. COUNT 15 GUILTY. Child M, allegation of attempted murder. Prosecutors said Letby injected air into the bloodstream of Child L’s twin brother. COUNT 16 GUILTY. Child N, three allegations of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby inflicted trauma in the baby boy’s throat and also injected him with air in the bloodstream. COUNT 17 GUILTY, COUNT 18 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT, COUNT 19 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT. Child O, allegation of murder. Prosecutors say Letby attacked the triplet boy by injecting him with air, overfeeding him with milk and inflicting trauma to his liver with “severe force”. COUNT 20 GUILTY. Child P, allegation of murder. Prosecutors said the nurse targeted the triplet brother of Child O by overfeeding him with milk, injecting air and dislodging his breathing tube. COUNT 21 GUILTY. Child Q, allegation of attempted murder. The Crown said Letby injected the baby boy with liquid, and possibly air, down his feeding tube. COUNT 22 JURY COULD NOT REACH VERDICT

Letby’s legal team, headed by barrister Mark McDonald, has submitted an application to the Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC), which could see Letby’s case referred back to the Court of Appeal and her convictions quashed.

Letby, formerly of Hereford, has always maintained her innocence.



She was twice denied permission to appeal against her convictions in 2024.

In February last year her new legal team presented reports from a panel of 14 international experts which, they say, casts doubt on the jury’s guilty verdicts.

A public inquiry, led by Lady Justice Thirlwall, into how the neonatal nurse was able to commit her crimes is due to publish its findings later this year, on a date yet to be announced.

We reported how both inmates spend hours trying to out-manoeuvre each other into checkmate on the jail unit.

News.title: Cancer-causing asbestos found in popular Amazon toy sold in UK as shoppers warned ‘stop using immediately’
News.content:
A POPULAR sand toy has been pulled from Amazon over fears it contains asbestos.

Users have been urged to stop using the sand bottles immediately, and to contact their local authority for disposal advice.



Craftplay Sand Art Bottles, sold in a pack of 10, have been recalled by Amazon‘s marketplace as it was found to pose a health risk.

Sand inside the bottles were found to be contaminated with small quantities of asbestos, causing it to be pulled from sale.



The sand art bottles, manufactured by Anthony Peters Mfg Co Ltd, were said to have originated in China with the Amazon code B0B15J7N2B.

Recall information published by the OPSS is yet to specify how long this sand art kit was on sale before it was recalled by Amazon.



Over the past seven months, 183 other asbestos-contaminated craft kits, children’s toys, and novelty doorstops have been pulled from shelves, with a long list of renowned British retailers impacted.

This includes seven other sand art bottles and craft kits, sold and distributed by Habico Ltd, Kids Create, KTL (Kandy Toys), and more.

For any product containing asbestos, the owner should stop using them immediately.

If the sand is still in its packaging, it must be placed in a heavy-duty plastic bag, double-taped, labelled and stored out the reach of children.



When the sand has been used, sites where it has spilled should be cleaned using wet cloths, wearing gloves and a mask – then, the cleaning equipment must be bagged securely in the same way.

Children should be kept away from the affected areas until they are completely clean.

Amazon has yet to publish any information regarding refunds, so the OPSS has directed customers to contact their local authority for information on how to safely dispose of asbestos.

It has been illegal to import, export, sell, or use any forms of asbestos in the UK since 1999 due to well-known evidence that the substance is harmful, even in small quantities.

News.title: First pic of ‘incredible’ schoolgirl, 9, who died in Arbroath as dad arrives at court over her death
News.content:
A SCHOOLGIRL allegedly killed after camping with her family at an industrial estate in a Scots seaside town has been named.

Minnie Merriman, nine, was found seriously injured at the Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath, Angus, shortly after midnight on Monday.



The youngster – described by devastated loved ones as their “beautiful and brave Minnie Moo” – was rushed to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee, where she sadly passed away.

The child’s dad was charged in connection with her death and arrived at court on Wednesday morning.



The 35-year-old, of West Yorkshire, was led into Forfar Sheriff Court in cuffs by officers.

The suspect was arrested and charged after police launched a “suspicious” death probe into Minnie’s passing.

In a statement, released through Police Scotland, Minnie’s heartbroken family said: “We are devastated with the loss of our beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo. Our family asks that our privacy is respected at this extremely difficult time.”

Detective Inspector Mike Ness of the Major Investigation Team said: “Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by these events, especially Minnie’s family.



“A police presence will remain in the area while our enquiries continue.

“Anyone with any concerns, or information, should approach these officers or contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 0008 of Monday, 3 August 2026.”

We previously told how Minnie was discovered fatally injured at the industrial park after a family ‘camping’ trip which led them to pitch a tent within the estate.

Witnesses told how they were seen cooking on an outdoor stove by the roadside less than a mile from the seafront just hours before she was found injured.

Locals told of their surprise at seeing the makeshift camp on the edge of an oil firm’s car park, a short distance from the beach, on Sunday evening.



Emergency crews swarmed the area after the alarm was raised just before midnight on Sunday.

Minnie was rushed to hospital along with three other patients before she died.

Her dad was taken to the same hospital separately but was later released into police custody before being charged in connection with her death.

Forensics officers were seen looking inside the car while an incident tent is believed to have been covering the family’s shelter.

Shocked local residents have been visiting the site where Minnie was found to lay floral tributes.



More to follow…
