News.title: Russian drone boss wounded & driver killed in car blast 1,300 miles from Ukraine as dramatic vid shows Mercedes on fire
News.content:
A RUSSIAN drone boss and top Putin crony has been severely wounded in a massive car blast 1,300 miles from Ukraine.

A driver and bodyguard were killed after the Mercedes of Vladimir Tkachuk, 35, was blitzed, leaving the warmonger fighting for his life.



Shocking images show the burnt-out carcass of Tkachuk’s luxury ride on the streets of the quiet Bolshoy Istok village in Yekaterinburg.

Dramatic footage shows plumes of black smoke pouring from a raging fire at the blast site.



A witness said: “A loud explosion was heard before a fire. It’s unclear what it actually was. But it’s scary.”

Tkachuk serves as CEO of Ural Drone Plant, which provides killer Upyr – or Ghoul – unmanned planes to Russian forces.

The Putin crony also runs the propagandist Telegram channel Obsessed with War, which has amassed 660,000 followers.

He has even personally demonstrated his drones to the tyrant.



The Ghoul drones are a relatively inexpensive FPV kamikaze quadcopter designed to carry explosives into Ukrainian troops, trenches and armoured vehicles.

His company is working on a heavier drone for the Russian Defence Ministry.

The blast is believed to have come from an explosive device fitted to Tkachuk’s car.



It comes just days after a major explosion at an elite Moscow restaurant hosting a Putin general’s lavish birthday bash killed five people.

Among the dead was Daniil Peredriy, 27, son-in-law of the intended target Alexander Chayko.

A homemade explosive device hidden inside a birthday gift detonated on the restaurant’s veranda.

Chayko escaped the blast unhurt, but his 25-year-old daughter Maria reportedly suffered a “traumatic brain injury”.

Former professional ice hockey player Peredriy married Chayko’s daughter in June last year.



The couple had organised the lavish £85,000 birthday celebration for her dad on Saturday.

The exclusive Balzi Rossi restaurant was packed with senior Kremlin insiders, high-ranking military officers, FSB agents and government officials.

The female courier may have been unaware she was carrying an explosive device capable of being detonated remotely.

Chayko was appointed commander of the Russian Aerospace Forces in May 2026.

Ukraine has designated him a wanted “war criminal” over his alleged role in commanding Russian troops responsible for the 2022 Bucha massacre.



Russian forces under his command are accused of carrying out mass rapes, torture and executions in the town, just west of Kyiv, during the opening weeks of Putin’s full-scale invasion.

More than 450 civilians were killed in what is widely regarded as one of the worst atrocities of the war.

It comes as another senior Russian commander was reportedly killed by a Ukrainian FPV drone.

Major General Dmitry Mikhailov, 39, one of Putin’s youngest generals, is said to have suffered fatal injuries while travelling in an armoured Tigr vehicle.

He had allegedly ignored repeated warnings about the threat posed by Ukrainian drones before entering the combat zone.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mikhailov has also been accused of war crimes during Russia‘s occupation of the Izium region, with Ukrainian investigators naming him among those responsible.

More than a dozen Russian generals have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

News.title: Two teen boys, 15 & 17, arrested after girl ‘forced into vehicle’ at Tesco car park in horrifying ordeal
News.content:
HORROR ORDEAL Two teen boys, 15 & 17, arrested after girl ‘forced into vehicle’ at Tesco car park in horrifying ordeal

TWO teenagers have been arrested after a teen girl was reportedly abducted outside a Tesco car park in a horrifying 40-minute ordeal.

A 15-year-old boy and a 17-year-old boy have detained on suspicion of false imprisonment after a teen girl was “forced into a car” in Church Langley, Essex.

The girl was allegedly driven to Epping after she was bundled into the vehicle around 6.50pm on Monday, where she managed to escape and flag help at around 7.30pm.

Essex Police have since launched a probe and are appealing for any witnesses to the incident which started in Minton Lane car park, Church Langley.





The alleged victim managed to get out of the car in Buckingham Road at the junction with Lower Swaines, Epping.

Two teen boys aged 15 and 17 were arrested today and have since been released on bail as police continue enquiries.

Cops confirmed the teenage girl is back with her family and being supported by specialist officers.

Detective Sergeant Paul Marks said: “We understand this incident has caused concern in the community and I’d like to thank everyone who has come forward with information so far.



“Based on our enquiries to date, we do not believe there is an ongoing threat to the wider public.

“The victim continues to be supported by specialist officers while our investigation continues.”

Anyone with information is urged to contact the force quoting incident 1362 of 3 August.

A spokesperson for Essex Police said: “We were called on the evening of Monday 3 August to a report of a teenage girl being forced into a vehicle in Church Langley.



“The incident is reported to have started in the Minton Lane car park at Tesco shortly after 6.50pm.

“The vehicle then travelled to Epping, where the girl reported getting out of the car in Buckingham Road, at the junction with Lower Swaines, at around 7.30pm.

“On Tuesday 4 August, a 15-year-old boy and a 17-year-old boy were arrested on suspicion of false imprisonment.

“They have since been released on bail while our enquiries continue.”

News.title: UK single-sex policy branded 'chaotic and cruel' as it comes into force today
News.content:
The updated Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) code comes into force in the UK today (August 5), despite over 160 MPs signing a 'prayer' motion to block it - including more than 90 Labour backbenchers defying the policy. The code has also faced backlash from trans organisations across the UK, who say it's a major back step for trans rights.

The updated code addresses a variety of scenarios from sport, where it states trans people should compete alongside others of their birth sex rather than gender identity, to hospital wards, which it says can lawfully exclude trans patients if single-sex.

Alexandra Parmar-Yee, Director at Trans+ Solidarity Alliance, called for the law to be changed to protect trans people’s ability to go about our day to day lives safely and with confidence.

"The Code of Practice has already caused serious harm to trans people across the UK, and these harms will only increase with implementation. Trans people will be shut out of the services they need, made to feel unwelcome and unsafe in public spaces. Our lives will feel smaller and more precarious," she said.

‌



View 2 Images The code of practice comes into force today

LGBT+ charity urges MPs to act fast on conversion therapy ban after years of abuse READ MORE :

"Organisations of all kinds have been left with no clear or safe route for inclusion and will be stuck in the crossfire of lawfare. The legal framework that protects all of our human rights has been fundamentally undermined.

"This is the UK Government’s flagship policy for the trans community, and it is chaotic, unworkable and cruel. It leaves the UK an outlier, no longer living up to its human rights commitments. It must change for the UK to once again be considered a nation that protects the human rights of all LGBTQ+ people," she concluded.

Good Law Project’s trans rights lead, Jess O’Thomson said: “It’s difficult to believe just how far backwards our government has gone on trans human rights.

‌



"This Labour government pushed through its transphobic guidance in the face of opposition from many MPs, including nearly a hundred of its own backbenchers. It’s not just immensely harmful. We think it’s unlawful, and completely against human rights."

As part of their statement, Trans Advocacy and Complaints Collective said: "We refuse to accept a future in which our rights are dismantled piece by piece while those responsible insist that nothing fundamental has changed. Our rights are not a political bargaining chip. Our lives are not up for debate. Our existence is not something that can be negotiated away."

"Equality was never supposed to be something that needed defending but history has shown that rights survive only because ordinary people refuse to surrender them. We intend to be those people."

What's included in the EHRC updated guidance?

The code of practice for services, public functions and associations, spanning more than 300 pages, encompasses nine protected characteristics including age, sex, disability, race and gender reassignment, and has been comprehensively updated for the first time since 2011.

‌



The updated guidance has been released more than a year after a landmark Supreme Court judgment in April 2025, which ruled the words "woman" and "sex" in the Equality Act 2010 refer to a biological woman and biological sex.

It indicates it can be considered legitimate, in limited circumstances, to request someone to confirm their sex, though this must be done "as sensitively as possible, and must respect their privacy".

Regarding toilets, the code states that it would be "very unlikely to be proportionate to put a trans person in a position where there is no service that they are allowed to use".

It states it is "unlikely to be either practical or appropriate to approach any particular individual to make enquiries about their sex in relation to facilities, such as toilets, which are incidental to the primary service".

‌



What's the Government's response to the EHRC guidance?

In May, Women and equalities minister Bridget Phillipson said the Supreme Court ruling had "made it clear that sex means biological sex" under the Equality Act, "and that trans people are still protected by the Act".

As the new code came into force, a Government spokesperson told The Mirror: "The government is committed to upholding single-sex spaces while protecting the rights of trans people. There are clear laws in place to protect trans people from discrimination and harassment, which we continue to uphold.

"We have strengthened protections for trans people against hate crime and just a month ago published our trans-inclusive conversion practices ban, as well as promoting LGBT+ rights internationally and improving LGBT+ healthcare."

If you have been affected by this story, contact Mindline Trans+'s emotional and mental health support helpline for anyone identifying as trans, non-binary, gender variant, and their families, friends, colleagues and carers. Their phone line is open Mondays and Fridays, 8pm to midnight. Ring 0300 330 5468.

News.title: Ramipril and amlodipine warning to anyone who takes them for blood pressure
News.content:
Ramipril and amlodipine warning to anyone who takes them for blood pressure

The NHS GP appeared on Lorraine to share a warning to users over the possible side effects and what can be done

View 2 Images Ramipril is one of the most widely prescribed blood pressure medications in the UK (stock image) (Image: Getty)

Dr Amir Khan has issued a new warning to anyone prescribed ramipril and amlodipine for their blood pressure. The NHS GP appeared on ITV's Lorraine to discuss what people taking the medication must be aware of, including side effects, and shared a clip from the episode on his Instagram account today (August 5).

‌



He told his followers: "If you're on blood pressure tablets: watch this". In the caption, he added: "Blood pressure medication is lifesaving for so many people - but common blood pressure tablets like ramipril and amlodipine do have side effects, which either mean people suffer in silence or stop taking them altogether."

‌



He continued: "But we have plenty of alternatives - so if that’s you, please discuss with your local pharmacist or GP who can help." In the clip, Dr Amir Khan says that the two most common blood pressure tablets are ramipril and amlodipine.

‌



The health expert said ramipril works by influencing enzymes in the kidneys to lower blood pressure. But he says it also releases something called bradykinin, which can irritate your airways and cause a dry cough.

"Lots of people get put on antibiotics and get sent for chest X-rays, and nothing gets found," Dr Amir Khan explained. "It's the ramipril. There are lots of alternatives."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



As for amlodipine, Dr Amir Khan warned about its potential effects on some users. He said: "The way [amlodipine] works is by widening your blood vessels and allowing some leakage of fluid into your ankles - you get swollen ankles."

He said this is "very common" and can effect "one in five people". He went on to reiterate: "So, again, lots of alternatives to blood pressure tablets, we've got different options. If you're suffering with swollen ankles or a dry, irritating cough, it could be your blood pressure tablets. Speak to your doctor. Plenty of alternatives."

In the comment section, one viewer claimed: "Amdopipine can also cause drug induced hyperplasia in your gums as a side effect so make sure you have healthy ones before starting this medication to limit risk of this occurrence." Another shared: "My husband couldn’t tolerate ramipril or amlodipine (swollen ankles) currently takes losartan (ARBs). BP Perfect."

‌



View 2 Images Dr Amir Khan said some patients may not realise it could be their medication causing the side effects - like a dsry cough (stock image)

Always speak to your doctor if you have any issues or concerns with your prescribed medication. If the side effects are bothering you, there are likely other options to consider instead.

Around one in three adults in the UK, which is about 14 to 16 million people, suffer from high blood pressure. Among this group, around five to six million are unaware that they have high blood pressure, as they have not been diagnosed, as it usually shows no symptoms at all.

‌



What are the common side effects of ramipril?

The NHS says a dry, persistent cough that does not get better is a side effect of ramipril. It says: "Cough medicines do not usually help for coughs caused by ramipril. Sometimes the cough gets better on its own if you keep taking ramipril."

These common side effects of ramipril happen in more than one in 100 people. There are things you can do to help cope with them:

Feeling dizzy or lightheaded, especially when you stand up or sit up quickly

Headaches

Diarrhoea

Being sick

A mild skin rash

‌



The NHS adds: "Talk to your doctor if it carries on, bothers you or stops you sleeping, as another medicine may be better... Like all medicines, amlodipine can cause side effects, although not everyone gets them. Some side effects should ease after a week or so as your body gets used to the medicine, but others can last longer."

What are the common side effects of amlodipine ?

swelling in your ankles, feet and legs

headaches, dizziness and feeling sleepy

a fast heartbeat, or feeling like your heartbeat is more noticeable (palpitations)

a red and warm face or neck

tummy pain and feeling sick

constipation or diarrhoea

feeling weak and tired

Article continues below

If you feel dizzy or sleepy after taking amlodipine, do not drive, ride a bike, or use machinery until these symptoms have passed. You can report any suspected side effect using the Yellow Card safety scheme. Visit the Yellow Card website for more information about reporting side effects.

News.title: Europe's 'worst EVER plastic nurdle incident' sparks huge 'People's Army' response on UK river
News.content:
Europe's 'worst EVER plastic nurdle incident' sparks huge 'People's Army' response on UK river

The Port of Tyne met with green campaigners for the first time this week, and was now backing a multi-agency clean-up “where safe to do so”, after a billion plastic pellets washed up

View 3 Images Some of the one billion plastic 'nurdles' which escaped into the water.

A "People's Army" is tackling - what has been described as - Europe’s worst ever nurdle pollution incident.

‌



Campaigners urged volunteers to help after a billion plastic pellets ended up in the River Tyne. The Port of Tyne met with green campaigners for the first time this week.

‌



The body is now backing the river clean-up, but only “where it is safe to do so”. It followed an open letter from the group, which wanted to remove the nurdles from beaches.

‌



The ‘Nurdle Clean Up Communities’ of North Shields, South Shields, Northumberland and Sunderland, combined more than 2,000 signatures. Their letter went to Port of Tyne CEO, Matt Beeton. Thousands of volunteers have since turned out to collect the pellets on beaches.

View 3 Images Plastic nurdles collected on Longsands Beach in Tynemouth.

Spokesperson Katie Bryson said: "Sadly it was the only way they would get cleaned up. The authorities were saying 'don't do it,' but Surfers Against Sewage urged their members to act. Thousands of people have been down on their hands and knees clearing up the beaches."

‌



The group has expressed its “outrage” over what it deemed the Port Of Tyne’s “inadequate response” to the incident on Sunday July 19. It involved a collision between two ships and the collapsing of a gantry crane. One port worker was taken to hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

An estimated one billion nurdle plastic pellets spilled into the water from one of the vessels involved in the incident. Nurdles are tiny disc-shaped plastic pellets that act as the raw material to manufacture most plastic products.

View 3 Images Members of the North Tyneside community gather at Whitley Bay beach for the clean-up

‌



Animals can easily mistake them for food with deadly consequences, campaigners say. The environmental charity Fidra, which worked to end plastic and chemical pollution, said nurdles were a global problem. Last year it found plastic nurdles at 84% of the UK’s sites of special scientific interest.

The Port of Tyne, HM Coastguard, the Environment Agency, local councils and specialist contractors were all involved in what has been called “a coordinated multi-agency effort” to clean up after the spill.

Port of Tyne Chief Executive Matt Beeton welcomed community volunteers in a meeting on Monday.

Article continues below

Mr Beeton said: “It was fantastic to begin a dialogue that will be so important as we all come together in the continued cleanup operation. In that sense the meeting strengthened those relationships as we work together for the best outcomes for the whole region.”

He added: “It has been a complex and difficult two weeks. I am proud of our staff for the way they have responded to what was a traumatic event. It was great to speak to local people to share what happened and help them understand how we responded and why.

"Now that the salvage operation has passed a critical stage, we are putting plans in place to invite the community to help in a safe and managed way. The solution will be in conversation with volunteers who will play a major role in deciding what we do and how we do it, as well as taking part in the continued cleanup."

News.title: UK weather maps show possible hottest day of year as 8 counties hit 37C or more
News.content:
UK weather maps show possible hottest day of year as 8 counties hit 37C or more

Temperatures in some parts of the UK could surge past 37C once more next week, as Met Office weather forecasters say conditions may turn ‘very warm or hot’ once again

View 3 Images Anomaly maps show temperatures will soar above the seasonal average next week (Image: WXCHARTS)

Weather forecasting models show the UK could see the hottest day of the year so far next week.

‌



The current temperature record for 2026 stands at 37.7C, which came on June 26 in Lingwood, Norfolk. However, temperatures could rise past 37C again next week, data suggests.

‌



The GFS weather model shows maximum temperatures reaching 34C on Wednesday next week in southern England, in an area stretching from Gloucestershire to Surrey. South Wales could hit 31C, while the Midlands may rise as high as 33C.

‌



Highs of 36C are possible quite widely across western and southern England on Thursday next week, the model shows, with temperatures climbing to 33C in areas as far north as Yorkshire, and 28C in southern parts of Scotland.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) on August 13 (Image: WXCHARTS)

UK weather maps show 10 counties reaching 36C or more in new heatwave next week READ MORE :

Met Office names 6 areas facing hail and lightning in new warning – full list READ MORE :

Western England and south-east England could then see highs of at least 37C on Friday next week. The model shows 36C is possible quite widely across central England and southern areas.

‌



For Saturday next week, maps show potential highs of 36C in East Anglia, 33C in Yorkshire, 36C in the south-east, and 33-34C in the Midlands. This hot spell would constitute another official heatwave across the four days.

Temperature anomaly maps for next week show the UK shaded in areas of deep red. This indicates where temperatures will rise well above the seasonal average.

View 3 Images Maximum possible temperatures (C) on August 14 (Image: WXCHARTS)

‌



In total, the GFS model suggests temperatures may reach 37C or more in eight counties next week. They are all in England.

UK counties facing 37C next week

Worcestershire

Warwickshire

Gloucestershire

Buckinghamshire

Berkshire

Hampshire

Surrey

Sussex

Met Office weather forecast

The Met Office says conditions could potentially turn ‘very warm or hot’ again later this month. However, there is also the potential for some ‘thundery interludes’.

Article continues below

The Met Office forecast for August 9 to 18 states: “Further into August, high pressure may become more dominant towards the north or northwest of the UK, with lower pressure to the south or east.

“This means there is a greater chance of frontal systems or thundery interludes to affect southern and eastern areas in comparison to recent weeks, though rainfall amounts could be quite variable with some areas still seeing relatively little.

“For the most part, temperatures look to remain above average, especially in the south, and perhaps turning very warm or hot.”

News.title: Woman who left UK for Spain says she won't come back for tragic reason
News.content:
Woman who left UK for Spain says she won't come back for tragic reason

A British woman who moved from London to Spain has explained why she won't come back and why she's going to move ot another European country instead

View 3 Images A woman who moved to Spain has explained why she won't retun to the UK (stock) (Image: Gonzalo Azumendi via Getty Images)

A British woman who left the UK to live in Spain has explained the tragic reason why she won't return to the UK, despite the danger from the wildfires and extreme heat rapidly sweeping a nation she has called home for the past three years.

‌



Former accountant Barbara, 72, has lived in the Spanish city of Granada since she left London for warmer weather and increased levels of sunshine.

‌



However, she has since expressed her regret about the move due to the extreme temperatures that have left her stuck inside her rented property.

‌



In fact, the heat has become so acute that she has considered moving to Portugal instead to try and escape the blazing temperatures and risk of wildfires.

This is instead of returning to the UK, which, while facing its own wildfire risk, is not subject to the same harsh conditions as Spain and France are currently facing.

View 3 Images Barbara said why she won't return to the UK (Image: Richard Baker, In Pictures via Getty Images)

‌



Explaining why she won't return to the UK, Barbara told the i newspaper: "Going back to the UK is not an option. I have no family. My husband died six years ago, as have most of my closest friends.

"I have friends in Portugal, they say summers there are very pleasant and bearably hot, with a constant fresh sea breeze along the Atlantic coast. I am planning a trip to Lisbon in November to start looking for houses to rent."

Barbara went into greater detail about how she feels about her move to Granada, describing it as the "biggest regret" of her life as she also described the fear she felt that her region would also be hit by the devastating fires that have cost the European continent millions.

‌



It is the ferocity of these wildfires that has caused such consternation as they have ripped through parts of Spain, France, and other European countries.

View 3 Images Spain has been devastated by the wildfires (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

It has been suggested that these wildfires have in part been driven by climate change which has seen temperatures regularly soar into the high thirties and early forties, putting massive pressure on ecosystems and the people within them.

Article continues below

Speaking to the Guardian about the matter, research associate at Imperial College London Dr Clair Barnes said that climate change was driving the dangerous phenomenon, a trend that was now playing out in real time.

She told the publication: "We’ve seen repeatedly how climate change increases hot, dry, flammable conditions that are extremely conducive to wildfires.

"It’s still early in the season – and with another heatwave looming, these findings are extremely scary. What we’re seeing is a clear sign of the escalating impacts of warming."

News.title: Girl, 9, who died while camping with family in Arbroath pictured as man, 35, due in court
News.content:
Girl, 9, who died while camping with family in Arbroath pictured as man, 35, due in court

A nine-year-old schoolgirl who died while camping with family in Arbroath has been named as Minnie Merriman

View 3 Images Minnie Merriman died after being found injured at an industrial estate in Scotland (Image: Police Scotland/PA Wire)

A nine-year-old girl who died after being found injured in Arbroath has been named as Minnie Merriman.

The schoolgirl was found seriously injured at the Elliot Industrial Estate just after midnight on Monday. She was rushed to Ninewells Hospital in Dundee but died from her injuries shortly after arrival.

Three other people were taken to the hospital and later released. A 35-year-old man has been arrested and charged in connection with her death.

Police said Minnie and the 35-year-old man are known to each other. He is due to appear in court today, Daily Record reports.

The girl's family were from West Yorkshire and had been camping in the area, police said.

View 3 Images Forensic officers at Elliot Industrial Estate in Arbroath (Image: Daily Record)

Her family said today: "We are devastated with the loss of our beloved, absolutely incredible, beautiful and brave Minnie Moo. Our family asks that our privacy is respected at this extremely difficult time."

Inquiries into Minnie's death remain ongoing. One witness said he drove past the family a few hours before the girl's death, where he reported seeing them cooking on an outdoor camping stove.

Another woman reported seeing a tent set up by a car, and commented that it was a "weird set up".

The industrial estate, which sits between a housing estate, a retail park and Arbroath seafront, is a busy area. Two caravan sites are also located nearby, although neither of them claim to have hosted the girl or her family prior to her death.

Local resident Bill Smith: "It's unbelievable. It's all everyone is talking about today as it's incredibly sad. Nobody seems to know what has happened. But it's tragic that a girl so young has lost her life here.

View 3 Images Floral tributes were left at the scene (Image: Daily Record)

"There's a path from the houses that goes through the industrial estate down to the shop. It's a busy area through the day."

A large cordon has been put in place around the crime scene while police conduct investigations. A blue electric Peugeot with a sunscreen covering the inside of the windscreen and a purple blanket blocking out the view from the rear was taped off by officers, while a blue forensic tent was also put in place.

Detective Inspector Mike Ness of the Major Investigation Team said: "Our thoughts remain with everyone affected by these events, especially Minnie's family.

Article continues below

"A police presence will remain in the area while our enquiries continue.

"Anyone with any concerns, or information, should approach these officers or contact Police Scotland on 101, quoting incident number 0008 of Monday, 3 August 2026."

News.title: Man who stabbed ex-partner 12 times in front of their child on busy street is jailed
News.content:
Man who stabbed ex-partner 12 times in front of their child on busy street is jailed

Osarenkhoe Atutie, 26, followed his estranged partner up to Edinburgh from London and brutally attacked her in the middle of a busy street

View Image Osarenkhoe Atutie (Image: Police Scotland/PA Wire)

A man who attempted to murder his ex-partner by repeatedly stabbing her in front of their daughter in the middle of a busy street has been jailed for seven-and-a-half years.

‌



Osarenkhoe Atutie, 26, previously admitted to brutally attacking his estranged partner Victory Atutie on Duke Street in the Leith area of Edinburgh on November 11 last year, leaving her with with 12 separate injuries and a collapsed lung.

‌



The attack was only stopped when three bystanders and intervened to stop the vicious assault, restraining Atutie on the ground and holding him in place until the emergency services arrived.

‌



During a sentencing at the High Court in Glasgow on Wednesday, Lord Cubie imposed a nine-year extended sentence on Atutie, comprising seven-and-a-half years in custody and 18 months of supervision on licence upon release.

“She could have died as a result of your actions," the judge said. "It is through a combination of luck and the intervention of three passers-by that she survived.

“They disarmed you and held you till police arrived and they are to be commended.”

‌



He added: “That the attack took place in front of your daughter is an aggravating factor. You seem to have a limited appreciation of the long-term effects this will have on your partner and child.”

Last month the court heard that Atutie met his partner in Nigeria, where they got married and moved to London before having a baby.

Ms Atutie moved to Edinburgh with the child following the breakdown of the relationship, while her estranged husband stayed in London.

‌



On the day of the attack, Ms Atutie had been taking her daughter to a doctor’s appointment when the 26-year-old approached them.

The court heard the child had seen him first and shouted “daddy, daddy”, and that initially Ms Atutie did not believe her as she thought he was in London. However, when she caught sight of him she “immediately panicked”.

The court heard Atutie came up to them and lifted the cover of the buggy before giving his daughter a hug, the court was told. He then told Ms Atutie: “I brought a knife, I will show you.”

‌



Prosecutor Catriona MacLeod said Ms Atutie continued walking, with Atutie alongside her. “The accused was angry, she was scared because she knew he was going to hurt her,” Ms MacLeod said.

At one point, Ms Atutie tried to get the attention of a man standing nearby, shouting: “He’s going to hurt me, he’s going to hurt me.” However, the man did not act, telling police afterwards Atutie had seemed “calm”.

He “grabbed her hair and repeatedly stabbed her in the head and body” during the horror attack. The knife was described as having a silver blade and being “around 10cm” in length.

‌



Following the attack, Ms Atutie was taken to hospital where as well as a collapsed lung she was found to have a haemothorax – fluid in the chest cavity – which the court heard can be fatal. She was discharged four days later, and although she made a full recovery she has been left with scarring at the site of her injuries.

At the hearing on Wednesday, defence advocate Jonny Campbell, representing Atutie, said. “He was struggling with his mental health at the time of the incident. That does not of course justify his actions.

“He has no previous convictions and he will now have a significant period of reflection to try and understand why he acted in this way towards someone with whom had had been in a long standing relationship.”

‌



He also said there is a significant chance Atutie will be deported.

Police Scotland Detective Sergeant Craig McMillan said after the sentencing: “This was a particularly harrowing incident, and my thoughts are with the victim and her family.

“I’d like to thank those members of the public who came to the victim’s aid during the ordeal. Without their intervention and assistance, there is a high chance that the victim would not have survived the attack.

Article continues below

“Tackling violence against women and girls is one of Police Scotland’s highest priorities and we continue to work with partners to achieve this."

News.title: 'Inconsolable' family lose everything as fires destroy Greece home days before leaving UK
News.content:
'Inconsolable' family lose everything as fires destroy Greece home days before leaving UK

EXCLUSIVE: Rory and his partner Stephanie were due to move their three children to Greece on August 10 before wildfires struck – now they're living in a one-bed flat

View 9 Images Stephanie and Rory with their three children Evangeline, Ivaria and Athena (Image: Stephanie Harper)

A heartbroken family have lost their dream home in the Greek mountains just days before they were due to leave the UK and move there permanently.

‌



Rory Clifford, 36, and Stephanie Harper, 35, built their perfect home in the mountainous region of Peloponnese, in the south of the country. Ahead of the dream move next week, they had shipped their sentimental belongings and enrolled their twin daughters, Evangeline and Ivaria, eight, in a local school for September. Stephanie is also currently pregnant with twins again and they also have a 19-month-old girl, Athena.

‌



However, fast-moving wildfires have swept through parts of Greece in recent days and it has resulted in their home and everything in it being destroyed.

‌



View 9 Images Their home has been gutted in the wildfires (Image: Stephanie Harper)

In an emotional interview, Stephanie told the Mirror: “We are a very resilient family but this has knocked it out of us completely. The emptiness and sorrow has been overwhelming.

“A dream and hard work not just from us but the Greek community who helped us achieve our home… just stolen in seconds. I can't describe the grief, as it's not just the house we built, it's all the cherished memories and the home we created inside.”

‌



The destruction of the property, which they bought in 2023, has meant that they are now in a one-bedroom flat in Hastings, East Sussex.

View 9 Images The beautiful home before it was ravaged (Image: Stephanie Harper)

They had spent well over €300,000 (approx £257,000) making it the ideal place to raise a family in the sun where they were also due to bring their three rescue dogs.

‌



Stephanie said the money came from their own hard work from running a designer furniture business together, as well as savings and loans.

The mum said they sold everything they had to make possible the relocation, which they had been planning for over a decade.

The process was long, stressful and came with many unexpected big costs, like spending over £10,000 replacing 2km of piping up the mountain in an effort to get water to the house.

‌



View 9 Images A GoFundMe has been set up to help the family (Image: Stephanie Harper)

Despite working day and night to jump over each obstacle, they are now cruelly left starting from scratch.

Since the devastating wildfire, Stephanie’s sister, Gabby, has started a GoFundMe to help the “inconsolable” family rebuild their lives.

‌



Stephanie said she was grateful and emotional about the response so far and she fears that even with insurance and cover, they need in the region of €100,000 (£85,000) to get back on track.

And regarding the fundraiser, she said: “Even saying this part makes us feel a little uncomfortable. We are not materialistic people and we don't want people reading about a pool, and thinking here we go, first world problems.

View 9 Images The couple are devastated about what has happened (Image: Stephanie Harper)

‌



“We live a very modest life, we have lived in a one-bedroom flat for 12 years, we have slept on a sofa bed for eight of those years, with our children having the bedroom. This Greek house was everything to us.

“It was a way of us affording a life we wanted to give our children, we spent every penny on giving our children the life they deserve and admittedly we were unbelievably excited to sleep in an actual bed. We will rebuild and we can't give up.”

Greece has always held a special place in the hearts of Stephanie and Rory who travelled there back in 2011 in a campervan.

‌



View 9 Images They made it an ideal home before they were due to move there this month (Image: Stephanie Harper)

The people left a mark on them and they began to envisage raising a family there.

Over time, the UK no longer felt like home, and with the cost of living crisis putting a strain on their business, they decided to make a bold and brave decision together.

‌



“Everything pointed to moving there,” Stephanie explained. “We just had to work it out. So that’s what we did and it took patience and a lot of research to make sure we had the right area.”

View 9 Images They are still coming to terms with the destruction (Image: Stephanie Harper)

That area turned out to be Peloponnese, a mountainous peninsula in southern Greece. The family spent eight weeks living there last summer and were able to picture what it would feel like doing so full-time.

‌



Since then, they have spent an enormous amount of time and money making sure everything was ready to move there permanently on August 10.

Stephanie had even been in contact with obstetrics to have her twins there at the start of 2027.

However, last Friday, a close friend who lives in a nearby village in Peloponnese told them that a wildfire was close to their region.

‌



It was something they experienced themselves last year and they noticed first-hand how incredibly fast the fire service was.

View 9 Images Stephanie pictured with her daughters (Image: Stephanie Harper)

On this occasion, though, their home could not be rescued. “We were helpless waiting for news. However, as darkness fell, helicopters can’t fly at night, so they’d have to wait until the first light. It took our house at 4am.”

‌



As for what the future holds for the soon to be family-of-seven, Stephanie said it was still early days and they were trying to figure out an action plan.

She said they were determined not to let it beat them, but admitted that keeping a positive mindset was challenging.

View 9 Images It has been a heartbreaking few days for Rory and Stephanie (Image: Stephanie Harper)

Article continues below

As for how their kids are coping, Stephanie added: “They have coped really well to be honest, it's hard for them to process as they were ready for the change and their next chapter.

“We will still do anything for our children's happiness and future which is why we can't give up on the House on the Mountain.”

To make a donation on the fundraiser, you can do so here

News.title: Police chief considers joining legal action over PC Harper killers' early release
News.content:
The driver of the vehicle, Henry Long, received a 16-year sentence and is not eligible for early release.

Speaking on the Today programme, Thames Valley Police chief Jason Hogg urged the government to reconsider its position.

Only prisoners convicted of murder, rape, grooming, and serious child sex offences will be excluded from the scheme in England and Wales - while those convicted of manslaughter remain eligible.

"I fully understand the challenges around the crisis in the prison system," he said.

"But the decision made and where that line has been drawn, I do not believe that people responsible for taking the life of another citizen in our country should be released early."

He said on Wednesday: "I was informed yesterday that the Police Federation are considering legal action, I am in discussions with the Police Federation with regards to this matter".

Asked whether this meant he would join them, he said: "I think we need to get some legal advice in relation to this. This is something I certainly would consider."

After campaigning by PC Harper's wife Lissie following his death, Parliament passed "Harper's Law", which gives mandatory life sentences to the killers of emergency services workers. It doubles the maximum penalty from 12 months to two years for those who assault police or other emergency workers.

But the new rules - introduced in 2022 - did not apply in the sentencing of the police officer's killers, and so do not prevent them from being released early.

Hogg said: "The law isn't retrospective and we all understand that, but the fact that they are released early simply seems perverse."

Aileen O'Connor, branch chair of Thames Valley Police Federation also told the BBC her organisation was considering legal action.

"We are in talks this morning, I'll get an update this afternoon whether that is an avenue that we can explore and if it is an avenue we can explore then I'll get behind that 110%," she told BBC Breakfast.

As for what shape a potential legal challenge might take, she said: "Ultimately that's for the specialists, the barristers and those in that legal sector to make that decision whether there is a challenge there.

"If there is a challenge then we will look to take that challenge."

Sentencing Minister Jake Richards told the BBC it would be wrong to pick out individual cases and block two of PC Harper's killers from early release.

Although the government had reviewed what sentences would be excluded from the early release scheme, he confirmed "manslaughter is not one of those offences".

Richards said: "It would be wrong to pick out individual cases within different offending cohorts. That wouldn't be right. It wouldn't be lawful either. So it is correct that those two individuals will be subject to the new regime from October".

On Tuesday Justice Secretary Alex Norris warned a prison capacity crisis would be likely if fewer prisoners were allowed early release.

Norris apologised to families who would be affected by the early release scheme and stressed that the government wanted to go further "but we cannot".

"We have to make this decision, we've been able to make some changes to it, but we have to have the rest of the sentencing act changes otherwise we run out of prison places in November and that can't happen," he said.

The justice secretary said 5,000 extra releases will take place in 10 batches from October.

Approximately 1,000 prisoners will now not be released early following the revision to the scheme, he clarified.

The government also announced an extra Â£10m will go to front-line victim support services, including a new national helpline.

On Wednesday the Ministry of Justice released a new list of exclusions that will be exempt from the early release scheme.

It said rapists, as well as criminals sentenced for child sex offences and grooming and conspiracy offences for these crimes, will no longer be eligible to leave prison early.

Murderers and terrorists were already not eligible for the early release scheme.

News.title: Ex-MP urges Tories to block council candidate jailed for antisemitic abuse against her
News.content:
A former Labour MP has said the Conservatives should not allow a former neo-Nazi who was jailed for antisemitic abuse against her to stand as a local election candidate.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine was convicted of racially harassing Luciana Berger, who is Jewish, in 2016, while already serving a separate jail sentence for sharing antisemitic posts.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has defended the decision to select him as a candidate in Somerset, saying that while his crimes were "appalling" he had been rehabilitated and was now "part of the fight against antisemetism".

But Baroness Berger said he should be barred from standing for public office - and Jewish groups have rejected a Tory invite to meet him.

Baroness Berger said Bonehill-Paine's harassment "affected my life in lots of different ways because of the volume of the material that he was disseminating and putting out, the extremity of it in terms of just frankly how shocking and awful it was".

The Labour peer added: "I think that we need to have a bar when it comes to standing for public office.

"I strongly believe that this individual today falls very, very short of that."

Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison after he was jailed in 2015 for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally.

A year later in 2016, he was convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Berger, a former shadow cabinet minister who is now a member of the House of Lords.

Baroness Berger attended court at the OId Bailey in London to give evidence in the trial of Bonehill-Paine.

In a Substack article, Baroness Berger said Bonehill-Paine had shown "no contrition" throughout the trial and claimed that at one point "he performed a full Nazi salute to his supporters in the public gallery".

"It told me everything I needed to know about how this individual saw the world, and about the utter contempt he held for the people he targeted," Baroness Berger wrote.

In sentencing remarks, the judge said it was "difficult to envisage a worse case than this of racially aggravated harassment of this kind", adding Bonehill-Paine had "sat in the dock smirking throughout the trial" and had "plainly enjoyed" Baroness Berger's discomfort.

The judge said in that in an online article, Bonehill-Paine described Baroness Berger as "a very evil woman" and doctored photographs of her into "sexualised images".

Baroness Berger resigned from Labour in protest at the handling of antisemitism allegations in 2019, before rejoining in 2023 after receiving an apology from former party leader Sir Keir Starmer.

News.title: Anthropic AI created fake profiles and impersonated people in attempted hack
News.content:
Two of the world's most powerful AI tools created fake human profiles to try and trick people in an attempted cyber-attack during testing by the UK's AI Security Institute (AISI).

In the most serious case, Anthropic's Mythos AI tried to gain access to a service by sending private messages, having set up fake accounts mimicking real people.

AISI said on Tuesday Mythos - and OpenAI's Sol - AI models had engaged in a level of "autonomy and deception" it had not seen before, though it clarified most of the malicious actions were carried out by Mythos.

Anthropic and OpenAI noted in response to AISI's report that its test had reduced or removed normal safeguards.

AISI evaluators first noticed "unusual data transfers leaving our research systems" during a test, then found that "some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations".

In the most serious case, a Mythos agent followed the routine of a human cyber-attacker by trying to trick people into giving it access to GitHub, a large platform where technology developers store software code.

The agent was trying to insert "malicious code" into GitHub's system.

It identified and researched the people who maintained GitHub and created a series of fake accounts based on those real people.

It sent messages and files through a file-sharing service as part of an effort to pressure and trick the people into approving its malicious code.

When challenged, "it edited its earlier activity to appear harmless and considered adopting a fresh identity to continue," AISI said.

Throughout the attempts, it was human review that stopped the agent from succeeding in delivering the malicious code to GitHub.

While AISI said the Mythos agent had not been instructed specifically to avoid or carry out such behaviour, it was "the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world".

The rival AI companies, which are poised to be listed on the public stock market, have been in the headlines in recent weeks after announcing their tools were responsible for several cyber-hacking incidents.

News.title: Family 'devastated' by death of girl, 9, injured on Scottish industrial estate
News.content:
The family of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured on an industrial estate in Arbroath said they are "devastated" at her loss.

Police have named her as Minnie Merriman from West Yorkshire. She died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on Monday.

Officers were called to the Elliot Industrial Estate shortly after midnight following reports that a child had been found injured.

A 35-year-old man, who was known to the girl, has been charged in connection with her death and is due to appear at Forfar Sheriff Court.

News.title: Traitors star Joe Marler to become BBC's first celebrity Gladiator
News.content:
Former rugby star Joe Marler is to become the first ever celebrity Gladiator on the BBC's popular entertainment series.

The 36-year-old, who also took part in the first series of Celebrity Traitors, will be known as Mauler and face contenders when the fourth series of Gladiators begins in 2027.

"Mauler will see you now," Marler said in a video posted on Instagram, external announcing the news, recorded in the Gladiators dressing room.

The BBC said Marler will make his debut with a series of "special appearances packed with power, personality and plenty of surprises".

Filming for the fourth series is currently under way in Sheffield, the BBC confirmed in a statement.

"Known for his uncompromising style of play and larger-than-life sense of humour, Joe has built a reputation as one of the UK's most entertaining sporting personalities," the corporation said.

"Now, he's taking on an entirely new challenge as he joins the ranks of the Gladiators, bringing his trademark physicality and competitive spirit to one of television's toughest arenas."

The former England rugby international star will join fellow Gladiators such as Nitro, Viper, Diamond and Sabre in batle when the show returns next year.

Gladiators was a hugely successful show on ITV in the 1990s, and saw members of the public take on a group of elite athletes who each had their own on-screen persona.

The format was revived by Sky for a single series in 2008, before the current iteration launched in 2024, quickly becoming a hit for BBC One.

A celebrity spin-off is separately in the works, featuring contestants including presenter AJ Odudu, comedian Sara Pascoe, podcaster Chris Ramsey and social media star George Clarke.

News.title: Misconduct proceedings against officer who shot Chris Kaba dropped
News.content:
The police officer who shot Chris Kaba will not face misconduct proceedings, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) has said.

Sgt Martyn Blake shot 24-year-old Kaba in Streatham, south London, in 2022 after he tried to ram his way past police cars. He was cleared of murder following a trial in 2024.

A decision was made in January to pause any proceedings involving Blake until a law change relating to the use of force in misconduct cases was introduced and its impact was clear, the IOPC said.

Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said the IOPC's decision brought an end to "almost four years of uncertainty" for Blake, calling the accountability process for police officers "disgraceful".

In June the use of force test in such cases changed from the civil law test to the criminal law test, meaning actions that did not amount to a crime should not amount to misconduct either.

Referring to Blake by his cypher NX121, Rowley said: "Today's decision finally brings to an end almost four years of uncertainty for NX121, his family and the wider firearms command, with all the considerable worry and stress that has brought.

"We also recognise the profound impact on Chris Kaba's family, who continue to grieve their loss."

News.title: Dewormer and scabies drugs being sold as cancer treatments, BBC investigation finds
News.content:
Animal dewormer and a drug used to treat scabies are being sold and promoted as unproven cancer treatments, a BBC investigation has found.

Following a tip off, an undercover journalist was able to buy fenbendazole and ivermectin from a stairlift salesman in south Wales, and also found them for sale on Amazon.

Macmillan Cancer Support said it was concerned by the findings and that a growing number of people were asking about the medicines, despite "no clinical evidence" that they work.

Amazon removed the products after we contacted them, and said it had "proactive measures in place" to stop prohibited products being listed by third-party sellers.

Senior doctors are worried vulnerable patients could be put at risk by taking the medicines, as they say it could harm or delay conventional treatment.

Six months ago, Rebecca Holder contacted the BBC after a visit from stairlift salesman Jason Sarver.

She said Sarver and her father Bob, who had a brain tumour, lung cancer and needed help with his mobility, had been discussing stairlifts when the salesman changed the topic to talk about the drugs.

News.title: Couple woke to find shirtless intruder in Travelodge room
News.content:
A couple woke to find a shirtless man in their hotel bedroom after he was mistakenly given a key card to their door, BBC Scotland News has learned.

Kim Hutchison, 60, and Harry Grieve, 57, from Buckie, Moray, were staying in a Travelodge in Dundee when the early morning incident happened last month.

Hutchison said she was "petrified" before the man - wearing just shorts - left after about a minute of arguing over who was actually in the wrong room.

Travelodge apologised to the couple and said room access security policies were not correctly followed. It is the latest in a series of similar incidents at Travelodge hotels reported to the BBC.

Earlier this year, a man was jailed for sexually assaulting a woman in her hotel bed after Travelodge staff gave him a key card and her room number.

Kyran Smith had gone to the reception of the Maidenhead branch of the hotel chain in the early hours in December 2022 and said he was the woman's boyfriend.

Travelodge later said it was investigating more reports of strangers accessing rooms - after two women told the BBC that people they did not know came into their rooms while they were alone.

News.title: Man gets third-degree burns from hot sand after using disposable beach BBQ
News.content:
Warning: This article contains a distressing image

A man who suffered third-degree burns from hot sand after using a disposable barbecue on a beach has warned others to be aware of the dangers.

Sam Knight had been using it on Cefn Sidan Beach, Carmarthenshire, with his family and stepped on sand that was still hot.

The 27-year-old had to be carried off the beach after suffering badly blistered feet and needed weeks of treatment.

Experts at a burns centre say injuries such as this are becoming increasingly common and warned beach goers to take precautions.

Knight told Radio Wales Breakfast he was not aware that sand could be a "real hazard".

He had used tongs to move the barbecue to one side and extinguished it, so he thought it was safe.

"When I returned to the area, I stepped on a boiling hot patch of sand, and had to be carried off the beach," he added.

Knight was taken to Neath Port Talbot Hospital referred to a burns specialist.

"I couldn't walk for a couple of weeks so I had to take a fortnight off work," he added.

David Fligelstone and Menna Davies are physiotherapists who work with the burns centre at Swansea Bay University Health Board.

Fligelstone said the number of incidents they are seeing is "going up year on year".

"The key thing is that people don't understand is that sand stays hot for such a long time after a barbecue is moved," he said.

"When you look at the evidence it's always the sand that hasn't been cooled that ends up causing that injury."

Davies said injuries like this can be "quite painful" and need to be dressed for a "long period of time".

News.title: Temperatures to drop briefly ahead of potential new UK heatwave
News.content:
Temperatures are set to drop across the UK over the next few days, ending the latest heatwave that has affected some areas of southern and eastern England.

Humidity levels will fall too, which should cool down homes and make nights more comfortable for sleeping.

The change in conditions follows another historic day in a summer that has seen many long standing heat records toppled or tied. On Tuesday, the UK registered its 34th day of temperatures reaching 30C (86F) or higher in a calendar year, equalling the record set in 1995.

Forecasts suggest that this record is likely to be beaten as early as next week, with some showing the potential for a sixth heatwave to develop.

News.title: Vegetables to get smaller and more expensive due to hot weather, farmers warn
News.content:
This year's harvest could be the worst on record as farmers warn the exceptionally dry spring and summer could lead to "shrinkflation" in UK supermarkets.

England and Wales saw their driest July since records began 190 years ago, according to the Met Office, and a drought has been declared across large parts of the country.

The Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU) thinktank said the UK's cereals and oilseed harvest could be 2.5 million tonnes less than âearlier forecasts.

Tim O'Malley, the chairman of Nationwide produce, said it was "as bad as its ever been" and that shoppers will likely see higher prices or smaller vegetables in supermarkets.

The harvest of barley, oats and rapeseed, which are used in beer, breakfast cereals and vegetable oil, is estimated to drop to just 19.5 million tonnes, the worst since records began in 1984.

That is compared with a previous low of 19.8 million tonnes in 2020, and would cost farmers Â£390m in lost revenue, the ECIU estimated.

The crops are also used for feeding livestock, making them crucial across most of the food chain.

O'Malley said consumers could feel the impact in the vegetable aisle too, where grocers are likely to swap in smaller produce at the same price, which is known as shrinkflation.

"I think we're going to see shrinkflation," he told Radio 5 Live's Wake Up to Money.

News.title: Burnham failing public over heat threats, says Green leader
News.content:
Zack Polanski has accused Labour of a "dereliction of duty" in the face of this summer's heatwaves, as he urged Andy Burnham to take further action in response to recent wildfires and droughts.

In a speech, the Green Party leader said the threat to public health and food supplies posed the "biggest threat to this country since the Second World War".

Record temperatures in recent months showed the need for immediate measures, he said, such as publicly accessible "cool spaces" and financial support to help households heatproof their homes.

But Labour criticised the Greens' record on reservoirs and clean energy projects, accusing them of "repeatedly" opposing new developments.

This summer has been exceptionally dry and hot, with temperatures setting numerous records and drought conditions leaving water supplies under strain and prompting warnings from farmers about the impact on food supplies.

Speaking in central London, Polanksi said higher temperatures were posing a "threat to our way of life" on multiple fronts, whilst footage of wildfires across Europe were "frankly apocalyptic".

He called on Burnham, who entered Downing Street two weeks ago, to show greater urgency in response to high temperatures, as he criticised him for not holding an emergency government Cobra meeting on the issue.

"Extreme weather is now the new normal â and without action, the impact on the people of this country will be unimaginably grave," he said.

The leader of the Green Party of England and Wales added: "The response from our government is to pretend none of this is happening.

"It's an astonishing dereliction of duty from those whose first responsibility is to keep us safe".

News.title: Body found in search for boy, 13, missing at sea
News.content:
A body has been found in the search for a teenager who went missing off the East Yorkshire coast, police have confirmed.

Emergency services were called to the South Promenade, in Hornsea, at about 18:00 BST on Tuesday after reports that a 13-year-old boy had got into difficulty while swimming.

Police said an "extensive search operation" had involved teams from HM Coastguard, Yorkshire Ambulance Service, and Humberside Fire and Rescue. Crews from Hornsea Inshore Rescue and the RNLI also attended.

Ch Supt Phil Booker said: "This is an incredibly heartbreaking outcome, and our thoughts are with the boy's family and friends at this devastating time."

News.title: Afghan boxer appears in court in connection with death of Scottish woman
News.content:
The man suspected of killing a Scottish aid worker in Greece has appeared in court in Athens.

The body of Elisabeth Ross was found in a suitcase at an abandoned building on 18 July, days after she had been reported missing.

Sharif Ahmadzai, who is 26 and from Afghanistan, was told during the private court hearing that he faces charges of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences.

He made no comment and the case was deferred until Thursday, when it is expected that Ahmadzai will be formally charged.

Homicide with intent is equivalent to a murder charge in Scots law.

Ahmadzai was driven to court in a grey Hyundai i30 with blacked out windows for the hearing.

News.title: Burnham not actively considering Epstein inquiry, No 10 says
News.content:
Andy Burnham is not actively considering holding a public inquiry into the UK activities of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, Downing Street has said.

It comes after Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones told BBC Newsnight the prime minister was "looking into" the possibility of an inquiry into the alleged actions of Epstein and the former Harrods owner Mohamed Al Fayed.

Davies-Jones said the prime minister had agreed to meet Epstein's victims, and the BBC understand Burnham is considering whether to meet the survivors.

Davies-Jones resigned from former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer's government in May, later accusing his government of failing to listen to Epstein's survivors.

She was reappointed as victims minister when Burnham took office.

The confusion in government thinking came after Davies-Jones told BBC Newsnight on Tuesday evening that she had discussed holding a public inquiry into the alleged behaviour of Epstein and Al Fayed with the prime minister and cabinet secretary Dame Antonia Romeo during her re-appointment.

Asked whether an inquiry was now possible, Davies-Jones said: "We are looking at this, we are reviewing what is possible. Again, same with Harrods survivors."

She added: "I have been assured that the prime minister is taking this very seriously.

"He will meet with those victims and he is looking at what is possible, now he has access to all of the information as prime minister to see what action we can take."

After resigning in May, Davies-Jones told the Commons in June that people whose lives were devastated by Epstein's abuse have too often been reduced to a footnote.

News.title: New guidance on single-sex spaces comes into force
News.content:
Single-sex spaces open to the public, such as toilets and changing rooms, should be organised based on biological sex, according to official guidance that has come into force.

The code, published by Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), says trans people should use either gender-neutral facilities or the ones that match their biological sex, in places such as gym changing rooms or rape crisis centres.

The guidance was published in June but is now in place in England, Wales and Scotland - despite opposition among some MPs.

It comes 16 months after the UK Supreme Court ruled "sex" in equality law means "biological sex" rather than the gender someone identifies as.

Trans-rights campaigners have called the guidance unworkable, but groups that campaign for sex-based rights welcome the clarity it brings.

The guidance from the EHRC, the equality watchdog for England, Scotland and Wales, provides practical advice for services, public bodies and associations on how they should interpret the 2010 Equality Act.

It applies to organisations as diverse as cafes, leisure centres, public toilets, domestic violence shelters, bowls clubs and many more.

The code says where it is proportionate for facilities, such as public toilets and changing rooms, or services like a rape crisis centre, to be single sex then only those of the same biological sex should use them.

This means, for instance, a trans woman, a person born a biological male who identifies as a woman, should not use women-only facilities. And a trans man should not use men only facilities.

But the code also says it could amount to discrimination against a transgender person if they were forced to use services related to their biological sex. It says gender-neutral spaces are an alternative.

The Equality Act provides protections for people on the grounds of both biological sex and gender reassignment.

Transgender people argue they should be able to use services that align with the way they identify and live their life, rather than their biological sex.

In response, campaigners including some women's and gay rights groups say this undermines sex-based protections, particularly for women.

It is the tension between these two sets of rights that led to both the Supreme Court ruling in April 2025 and the publication of this updated guidance.

It suggests legal action on how the code is put into practice is likely. Both from trans-rights groups who think the guidance itself is wrong and from sex-based rights groups who will want to challenge any organisations who they believe are not following the code.

Progressive Abdul El-Sayed is on the precipice of a Democratic primary win in the race for Michigan’s Senate seat Wednesday morning, clinging to a narrow lead in an extremely tight race against centrist Rep. Haley Stevens.

A win for El-Sayed, a former public health official, would come as a shock to the Democratic establishment and to AIPAC, D.C.’s top Israel lobby group. Stevens, a moderate establishment-backed candidate, has received tens of millions of dollars from AIPAC in support of her campaign.

Votes continued to be counted Wednesday morning, and despite his narrow lead, El-Sayed appeared to be gearing up for the general election in November. He told MS NOW that his team was “focused on trying to figure out how we bring the party together” to defeat the Republican nominee, Mike Rogers.

Both El-Sayed and Stevens took the stage after midnight to share their optimism with supporters. Neither have ceded as the count remains close.

“Tomorrow, we begin to mend fences,” El Sayed said. “Whatever happens tonight, we have a responsibility to assure that we unite to make sure that Mike Rogers never sees the inside of the U.S. Senate.”

open image in gallery Progressive Abdul El-Sayed holds a narrow lead over centrist Rep. Haley Stevens Wednesday morning in extremely tight Michigan Senate race ( AFP/Getty )

During her late-night speech, Stevens told supporters: “We knew this was going to be a close race, and that’s exactly what we’ve got: a close race. But friends, I am feeling good about this race. I am feeling fired up,” according to the New York Times.

Even though the race had not been called yet Wednesday morning, El-Sayed sent out a fundraising email reading “We won.” He was declared the winner by NBC News, though other major media outlets, including the Associated Press and The New York Times, have not yet named a winner.

While many more progressive Democratic candidates have found success in the U.S. House primaries, including in New York and Denver, those cities are deep-blue cities, whereas Michigan is more mixed. However, a progressive victory in Michigan would indicate a more significant milestone for progressives.

open image in gallery Haley Stevens was backed by Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Senator Gary Peters ( Getty )

The primary will likely be decided by outstanding votes in Wayne County, Michigans largest county and home to Detroit, which has historically released results later than other counties.It was not immediately clear when officials expected votes to be completely tallied.

El-Sayed was in the lead as initial results came in Tuesday night, but Stevens started closing that gap as votes came in from Wayne County.

However, either El-Sayed or Stevens will face Rogers in the general election in November. Each candidate is looking to succeed Senator Gary Peters, the moderate incumbent who is set to retire.

Peters and Michigan Gov Gretchen Whitmer both endorsed Stevens, while El-Sayed received support from the Democratic Party’s progressive wing in Congress, including from Senators Bernie Sanders, Elizabeth Warren and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

With reporting by the Associated Press.

Rep. Max Miller publicly took the first questions from a reporter regarding the shocking claims made by his ex-wife in an ongoing court battle on Tuesday as he sat down for an interview with CNN’s Jake Tapper.

Miller is accused by his ex-wife of scalding her with hot water and physically abusing both her and their daughter, whom Miller’s ex-wife claims had her collarbone broken by the Ohio Republican congressman. Those claims, which he denied in a video message on Sunday morning, were first revealed publicly by Mother Jones, detailing court documents filed in a defamation case Miller is pursuing against his ex-wife. Her father, U.S. Sen. Bernie Moreno, echoed those accusations and told reporters on the Hill this week that his daughter lives in fear of Miller and what he might do.

The interview Tuesday was tense, though Miller never lost his temper, as Tapper repeatedly pressed him about heartwrenching statements his daughter was alleged to have made about him and the home where she stays with him temporarily as part of a shared custody agreement.

At one point, the anchor questioned whether he was being inconsistent in his own characterization of his daughter’s verbal abilities.

“There is a police report from the suspected child abuse incident in February involving your daughter, and that report details that the child protection team says that your child had a right clavicle fracture, and “a bruise that accompanies the injury that appears to be in a handprint and appears to have been inflicted,” Tapper told Miller.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller denied accusations of abusing his ex-wife, daughter, and former girlfriends on CNN ( CNN - The Lead with Jake Tapper )

”Your ex-wife stated to police that your child told her in the days leading up to the discovery of the injury, quote daddy kill you, and your ex-wife also said your child had said, ' Daddy angry and daddy's house is scary,” he continued.

“Jake, I wish you could talk to my beautiful baby girl. She can't string together sentences like that. She's two and a half years old,” the congressman responded.

Tapper then shot back: “You just told me that she had said that she was scared to go to mommy's house.”

“She is. I have video of it,” said Miller.

open image in gallery Rep. Max Miller is up for re-election in a district that leans Republican in just three months ( Getty )

open image in gallery Sen. Bernie Moreno, his former father-in-law, urged Miller to quit Congress and seek psychological help ( Reuters )

“But now you're saying that she's not capable of saying ‘Daddy kill you?’” asked Tapper. “I mean, it seems like she's either able to say one but not the other. That doesn't make sense.”

Miller responded: “Jake. To be very direct, this is incredibly disturbing...You have to look at the timing of everything that is taking place, right? What about due process?”

Miller would repeatedly insist throughout the interview that he’d been investigated for the claims made by his ex-wife, and found to be innocent. He had no explanation for why his ex-girlfriend Stephanie Grisham, a former Trump White House aide, was also accusing him of abusive behavior, though he denied them as well.

And Miller invoked the allegations of lewd and unconsensual sexual behavior leveled at Donald Trump during the 2016 election cycle as he vowed to stay in his race for re-election.

“There are now three women who have accused you of violent behavior. Are all three of these women who don't know each other lying?” asked Tapper.

“Yes,” said Miller. “In 2016, when Donald J. Trump faced the most extreme allegations in the world that hit him day after day after day...guess what? He stayed in and he was resilient.”

At another point in the interview, he turned to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth as he explained why the Daily Mail had obtained pictures showing syringes found in his bedroom. During recorded conversations with his ex-wife Miller released as part of a trove of documents related to his divorce proceedings over the weekend, his ex-wife can be heard accusing him of having a “drug problem”.

“This is testosterone replacement therapy. People are painting this as something that it’s not. Secretary Hegseth, who is the Secretary of War, just three weeks ago, allowed our entire military, who are males, to take testosterone replacement therapy. That's what I was doing. I have not been using any illegal drugs. This is nonsense.”

Miller is running for his third House term in a relatively safe Republican district in Ohio, but the nature of the allegations has some Republicans fearing his chances of holding the seat.

One of those Republicans is Trump himself. Now facing the first midterm cycle of his second term, the president is staring down the likely possibility of his party losing one or possibly even both of their twin congressional majorities to the Democrats in the fall. Miller’s shaky candidacy could make the Democrats’ path to taking the House an easier prospect.

Trump reportedly called Miller on Monday to express his doubts about the congressman’s candidacy, but Miller said Tuesday that he would remain in the race.

Complicating the matter for him is his former father-in-law, Sen. Bernie Moreno, a fellow Republican, who spoke to reporters this week about how his daughter Emily lives in “constant fear” of the congressman, and has urged him to drop out of Congress.

“This is truly the seventh level of hell,” Moreno told reporters on Monday. “This has been a horrific experience for my entire family.”

“My daughter lives in constant fear of this man, not like something that’s existential, but deeply in her heart, she fears what this guy is capable of,” he continued.

India’s government has given Mark Zuckerberg an ultimatum to apologise for Facebook’s brief removal of a video by prime minister Narendra Modi or lose the social platform’s safe harbour protection.

A parliamentary committee claimed that the removal of Mr Modi's video from Facebook last month was an "attack on democracy".

If Mr Zuckerberg did not apologise within three days, it said, the government would revoke Facebook's safe harbour clause, exposing the Meta platform and its executives to legal action, including criminal proceedings, over content posted on it. "Mark Zuckerberg will have to apologise,” the committee said. “Otherwise, a case may be filed.”

A video message by Mr Modi posted on Instagram on 23 July was temporarily restricted when it was later shared on Facebook.

In what was his first selfie-style video on Instagram, Mr Modi addressed ​the “cockroach” protests that forced the resignation of education minister Dharmendra ​Pradhan.

India summoned the American tech giant’s executives to lodge a complaint after the video with over 400 million views disappeared from Facebook.

“We have asked Meta to come in at the highest level and explain what is happening,” S Krishnan, secretary at the ministry of electronics and information technology, said on 30 July.

A Meta spokesperson said at the time the post had been blocked inadvertently.

The company told Indian authorities it had established new protocols for accounts of prominent persons to prevent such a situation from recurring, Mr Krishnan added.

On Wednesday, Meta executives met Indian officials for about 45 minutes to explain their position.

The information technology ministry, however, reportedly rejected the explanation as "not reasonable", saying that if the incident was indeed caused by a technical error then the company should strengthen its systems.

The sparring with Meta is ⁠the ​latest instance of Modi's government taking ​on Big Tech over content issues.

In July, the government had ordered Meta to remove child sexual abuse content from Instagram and sought an explanation over allegations that its platforms were promoting such material.

The action came after a BBC Eye investigation found Instagram was running paid adverts promoting child sexual abuse material in India. It found the ads used certain terms to take users to Telegram app channels where they were asked to buy such material.

At the meeting on Wednesday, Meta executives reportedly conveyed an apology from Mr Zuckerberg over the availability of child sexual abuse material and deepfake content on his social media platforms.

“Meta admitted that a lot of money was paid for boosting certain types of content,” Hindustan Times quoted unnamed sources in the ministry of electronics and information technology as saying. “They accepted that a lot of illegal content was being promoted. The paid promotion was carried out for a specific audience. They apologised and regretted the mistake.”

It could not be ascertained, the paper added, if Mr Zuckerberg had apologised for removing the prime minister’s video as well.
