The leader of the Green Party has called for fossil fuel producers to be made to finance firefighting helicopters, following a spate of recent blazes across the UK.

Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Zack Polanski issued a stark warning, declaring: “We are facing the biggest threat to this country since the Second World War.”

He also pressed Prime Minister Andy Burnham to “be truthful, be brave” and halt new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, specifically naming the Jackdaw and Rosebank fields off the Scottish coast.

Polanski was joined in central London by BBC Springwatch presenter Chris Packham, who advocated for policymakers to “criminalise irresponsible journalism” and implement a wildfire warning system.

Sseveral wildfires have erupted in recent weeks, including significant incidents at Dunwich Heath in Suffolk, Llanwonno in the Rhondda Valleys, South Wales, and within the Cairngorms National Park in Scotland.

Mr Polanski said since the blazes, ministers had produced “no emergency briefings, no new plan and precious little detail about how this government will protect people from the crisis”.

open image in gallery Green Party leader Zack Polanski during a press conference at Church House in central London ( PA )

He warned that “the sheer scale of the devastation is hard to comprehend”, but added: “We need to look it in the face because this is only a taster of what’s to come if we don’t act now.”

He continued: “We need a robust wildfire prevention strategy, a fire service with the resources it needs to tackle blazes when they come.

“And that must include firefighting helicopters when needed and not again ever seeing the shocking sight of requiring a charity to step in to contract a private firm to help fight fires.

“And this should all be funded by taxing the fossil fuel giants who are profiting from fuelling these infernos.”

Mr Polanski also called for water companies to be taken “into public hands” because “money is flowing out of our hands into the pockets of shareholders, just like water is flowing out of those companies’ leaky pipes in the middle of a drought”.

open image in gallery Smoke rises from the smouldering remains of a wildfire at Dunwich Heath ( PA Wire )

Speaking as if to Mr Burnham, the Green Party leader added: “I hope you will have the courage to be truthful, be brave and hold firm to your party’s commitment to no new oil and gas drilling in the North Sea, including both Rosebank and Jackdaw.

“Now, some will say we can’t afford to make these changes. These last few weeks are showing we can’t afford not to – we are facing an existential threat.”

Mr Packham said: “Is there a public wellbeing system in place which will tell people when there’s a risk of wildfire, so that they can be prepared to evacuate and have evacuation plans in place?

“Well, do you know what? There is.

“It’s available to the fire and rescue service but it isn’t available to the public because it’s deemed to be unreliable.

“Is it unreliable or is it just a bit too scary?

“We couldn’t even instigate a ban on disposable barbecues.”

open image in gallery Zack Polanski, left, listens to Chris Packham during a press conference at Church House ( PA )

The presenter and naturalist also called for a “transition to a plant-based diet”, warning athat nimal agriculture is a “leading driver of biodiversity loss”.

He continued: “We’ve got to address the mis- and disinformation and we’ve got to do that with positive information campaigns – we’ve got to have people’s minds on the front foot so they know what’s true before they hear the lies.

“Then they will question the lies.

“Otherwise, you know what happens if you tell a lie frequently enough? It eventually becomes the truth.

“And that’s what we’re suffering from.

“‘We can’t afford net zero’? We can’t not afford net zero, and we’re beginning to see that that’s the case.

“We’ve got to sort out the media.

“I’ve been fantasising this year that we could perhaps criminalise climate denial – we should certainly criminalise irresponsible journalism.”

Close the door, shut the windows and turn up the heating, and you have all the ingredients for a sick bedroom in your home – and you spend about eight hours in there every night.

Kitchens and bathrooms usually take the blame for stale air and damp. But researchers spent a winter monitoring airtight, naturally ventilated homes across Scotland. In more than four out of five homes the carbon dioxide (CO₂) in the air remained above the level considered a safe threshold for the entire night. Despite this, more than nine in ten of the occupants thought the air in their bedroom was good.

The reason is not the room. It is you. Awake in the living room, you are a thermostat with hands. When the air turns stuffy, you crack a window. When you feel cold, you close it. This correction stops in bedrooms once you fall asleep, and two things build up: the CO₂ you breathe out and moisture with it.

open image in gallery Kitchens and bathrooms usually take the blame for stale air and damp ( Google Gemini/iStock )

High levels of CO₂ act as a proxy for stale air. CO₂ levels are measured in parts per million (ppm), a unit of measurement used to describe very small concentrations of a substance.

A study examining 40 Danish bedrooms revealed a troubling threshold: when CO₂ levels reach 1,800ppm, participants’ cognitive function the following day suffered. And sleep quality starts to suffer well below that.

Recognising this risk, strict European standards allow living spaces to reach 1,350ppm above outdoor levels, while restricting bedrooms to just 950ppm above outdoor levels. For reference, CO₂ levels in fresh outdoor air are typically between 420 and 450ppm.

Between 2022 and 2025, I continuously monitored temperature, humidity and CO₂ data using sensors from around 200 Irish rooms in highly energy-efficient but airtight Irish social housing. The bedrooms spent roughly two hours every night in winter above unhealthy levels, while the living rooms next door were fine. The same bedrooms were fine again during summer. The likely reason is that people keep their windows shut in winter to stay warm and open in summer.

Serious health consequences

Two sleeping adults breathe out about a pint of water a night. I run a dehumidifier at home over the winter – it holds two litres, and from October onwards I empty it every other morning.

Moisture, when trapped indoors, settles on the coldest surface – usually, the window or the wall behind a wardrobe. A cold, damp surface in a warm, moist room is an ideal condition for mould to grow.

This is not just a cosmetic problem. Prolonged exposure to mould in a flat in Rochdale, a town in Greater Manchester, killed two-year-old Awaab Ishak in 2020. Consequently, Awaab’s law now legally compels social landlords in England to address damp and mould within strict, fixed deadlines.

Small children are the most exposed of any of us, their lungs and immune systems are still developing, and they sleep longer than adults.

Airing a room by opening the window clears the stale air and the moisture at once, but it lets the heat out. That is the trade-off between fresh or warm air.

The trickle vents (small slots built into window frames for background airflow) are often found shut after energy upgrades, and a 2024 Irish study of retrofitted homes found bedroom CO₂ higher after the work than before, with around half showing visible mould.

This feels like deja vu. After the oil shocks of the 1970s, offices were sealed and ventilation cut to save fuel, and the occupants got headaches, itching eyes and a fog that lifted only when they went home. It was called sick building syndrome. It’s the same – except nobody gets to go home from their bedroom.

Energy-efficient but sick buildings often cost society far more than they save. Renters sit in the middle of it, unable to carry out expensive building changes.

What to do

If an open window loses heat, at least keep trickle vents open. Leave the bedroom door ajar, which gives the moisture somewhere to go.

A generational practice and German daily ritual of Lüften is now popularised on TikTok as “house burping”. By throwing the windows wide open for ten to 15 minutes immediately after getting up, you rapidly purge the stale air and moisture while saving heat loss.

When it is extremely cold, even for Lüften, people often reach for a dehumidifier. These devices cost roughly between £90 and £300, and a typical dehumidifier draws around 250 watts and costs around 6p to 9p an hour to run.

About the author Lala Rukh is a PhD Candidate, Energy, University of Galway; Atlantic Technological University. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article .

Most dehumidifiers have a humidistat (a small electronic device used to measure and control the humidity) that you can set to a minimum target. A sensible target for a bedroom is 60% – the machine runs until the room reaches it, shuts itself off, and wakes again when the humidity creeps back up. Others run for a specified period, set as desired, or continuously.

Dehumidifiers are a genuine help for a cold, damp bedroom when there are few other options.

While none of this replaces a proper ventilation system, it changes what you breathe at night. For definitive proof of bad air quality in your bedroom, use an indoor air quality monitor. Seeing the hard data is often the best prompt to open a window, clear a vent, or switch on a dehumidifier.

News.content:

Taiwan kicked off annual military exercises on Wednesday aimed at simulating a response to a potential Chinese invasion of the self-governed island Beijing claims as its own.

The live-fire exercises will test the Taiwanese army’s ability to sustain 24-hour defence operations as well as counter China’s “gray-zone tactics,” which stop just short of open warfare.

Urban resilience drills will test the population’s response to a disruption in internet service.

The 10-day Han Kuang exercises are set to be held in various locations around the island. This year’s drills will test new, US-inspired communication methods including backbriefs – where subordinates explain to commanders how they plan to carry out assigned missions.

The communication drills are intended to encourage first-line fighters to be more self-reliant and effective in battle, experts say.

open image in gallery Soldiers conduct shooting training during the annual Han Kuang military exercises in Taipei ( AP )

Another focus of this year’s drills is that they will mobilise the largest ever team of reservists, more than 5,000 service members across two brigades.

Last year’s drills involved one brigade of more than 3,000 reservists.

The drills will test how quickly reserves can mobilise from peacetime standby mode to full active duty.

Another focus of the exercises, reflecting Taiwan’s longstanding emphasis on civil defence, are urban resilience drills. These will take place on different days in the major cities of Kaohsiung, Taichung and the capital, Taipei.

During the drills, mobile internet speed will be reduced for about 30 minutes to simulate telecommunications interference in case of an attack.

Military equipment being tested will feature the newly acquired M1A2T Abrams tanks. Taiwan procured 108 of the American-made tanks in 2019, the last batch of which arrived in April.

Taiwan sources most of its weapons from the United States, which is the island’s main informal backer in the face of territorial claims from China.

Beijing regards democratic Taiwan as a breakaway province, to be retaken by force if necessary. In recent years, it has ramped up a campaign of military pressure, which has involved sending military aircraft and warships near the island almost daily.

Taiwan’s parliament recently approved a $24.8bn supplementary budget bill for the purchase of US arms, which fell short of Taiwanese president Lai Ching-te’s proposal for a $40bn budget.

The island’s government is waiting on the US to greenlight a $14bn arms sale package to Taiwan, which has been held up for months.

US president Donald Trump and the US Congress earlier approved a separate, record-breaking $11bn package.

But after traveling to China in May, Trump described arms sales to Taiwan as a “good negotiating chip” with Beijing and refrained from approving the newest arms sales package to Taiwan.

The director of a factory supplying drones to the Russian military was badly wounded when his car exploded, news reports said Wednesday.

The state Tass and RIA Novosti agencies said that Vladimir Tkachuk was hospitalized in grave condition following the explosion late Tuesday in Bolshoy Istok just outside Yekaterinburg, 1,400 kilometers (about 870 miles) east of Moscow. It didn’t immediately give details of the explosion or say who could be responsible. There was no immediate comment from the authorities.

Tkachuk headed the Uraldronzavod factory that manufactures Upyr (Russian for Ghoul) drones. Tkachuk, a small-scale entrepreneur, set up a team of engineers that developed the Upyr and organized its production near Yekaterinburg, Russia’s fourth-largest city and a key industrial hub in the Ural Mountains

The Upyr, a cheap and simple first-person view drone, was hailed by troops for the protection it offers against jamming.

Russian authorities have blamed Kyiv for a series of bombings and other attacks against senior military officials after Moscow sent troops into Ukraine in February 2022.

The explosion followed Saturday's deadly bombing at an upscale Moscow restaurant, which the Russian Embassy in Rome blamed on Ukraine, describing it as an attempt to intimidate the Italian community in Russia. It said in a statement Monday that the attack on the Balzi Rossi restaurant killed five and injured 19.

The Russian Foreign Ministry reposted the embassy statement without comment, and Russia's security agencies haven't named the suspected culprits. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin has described the bombing as a “brutal terrorist act,” but did not say who was responsible.

Several Russian media outlets claimed the bombing targeted a Russian general who was celebrating his birthday at the restaurant. Some claimed that the general was Col.-Gen. Alexander Chaiko, who led the troops that made a botched attempt to storm the Ukrainian capital in 2022 and recently was appointed the chief of Russia’s aerospace forces. The claims could not be independently verified.

Princess Eugenie has announced the birth of her baby girl.

Eugenie, who is the daughter of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, announced the birth of her third child on Instagram on Tuesday.

She gave birth at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, on Monday evening, Buckingham Palace said.

The princess and her husband, Jack Brooksbank, are taking their time to decide on a name.

In a short post, Eugenie, wrote: “Jack and I are so excited to announce Baby Girl Brooksbank!!

“We are beyond in love with our girlie.”

open image in gallery Princess Eugenie announced the birth of her third child on Instagram on Tuesday ( Jack Brooksbank/Buckingham Palace )

The new arrival is the fifth grandchild of the former Duke and Duchess of York, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and Sarah Ferguson, after the birth of Princess Beatrice’s daughter Athena Mapelli Mozzi in January last year.

The birth of her baby girl follows Eugenie’s sons August and Ernest, but where does the new baby sit in line for the British throne?

1. Prince William, Prince of Wales

Prince William, 44, is first in line to the British throne after his father became king.

Formerly the Duke of Cambridge, William became the Prince of Wales after the Queen’s death. He is the first child of King Charles III and when he becomes king, his wife, Catherine (known as Kate), 44, the Princess of Wales, will be known as Queen Consort.

open image in gallery Prince William, 44, is first in line to the British throne ( Getty )

2. Prince George

Prince William and Princess Kate’s first son, Prince George, is second in line to the throne.

The 13-year-old will be known as King George VII when he becomes monarch one day, but until then, his parents want him to have as normal an upbringing as possible.

3. Princess Charlotte

After an amendment made to the Succession to the Crown Act in 2013 – which means eldest children, regardless of sex, will succeed the throne first – Princess Charlotte, 11, is third in line to the throne after her big brother.

Before the Act’s amendment, her younger brother, Louis, would have been ahead of her in the line of succession simply because of his gender. But if Prince George has children one day, they will slot in behind him in the line of succession.

4. Prince Louis

Prince Louis, eight, the third child of Prince William and Kate Middleton, is currently fourth in line to the throne after his older siblings.

5. Prince Harry

As the second child of King Charles III and the late Princess Diana, Prince Harry, 41, is fifth in line for the throne after his brother, nephews and niece. His wife, Meghan Markle, is not in line for the throne – much like the Duchess of Cambridge – but their two children are.

open image in gallery Prince Harry , pictured with Meghan Markle, is fifth in line for the throne ( AFP/Getty )

6. Prince Archie Mountbatten-Windsor

Archie Mountbatten-Windsor, seven, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s first child, is sixth in line to the throne after his father, uncle and cousins.

7. Princess Lilibet Mountbatten-Windsor

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex’s second child, Lilibet, five, is seventh in line to the throne. The toddler’s name is a nod to the royal family’s nickname for the late Queen Elizabeth II, and her middle name is Diana, after Harry’s late mother, Princess Diana.

8. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor

Effectively no longer a royal, the scandal-plagued 66-year-old is Queen Elizabeth II’s third child and King Charles III’s younger brother. Despite giving up his royal titles and honours, he is still eighth in line to the throne.

9. Princess Beatrice of York

Princess Beatrice, 37, who is the daughter of Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, is ninth in line to the throne.

open image in gallery Princess Beatrice, who has two children ( AFP/Getty )

10. Miss Sienna Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi

Her daughter, Sienna Elizabeth Mapelli Mozzi, four, whom she shares with her husband Edoardo Mapelli Mozzi, is 10th in line.

11. Miss Athena Mapelli Mozzi

Princess Beatrice’s second daughter, Athena Mapelli Mozzi, one, is 11th in line.

12. Princess Eugenie of York

Princess Eugenie, 36, Princess Beatrice’s younger sister, is 12th in line to the throne.

open image in gallery Princess Eugenie and Jack Brooksbank have three children (PA) ( PA Archive )

13. Master August Brooksbank

Eugenie’s son with husband Jack Brooksbank, August Brooksbank, five, is 13th in line.

14. Master Ernest Brooksbank

August is followed in the line of succession by his younger brother, Ernest, born May 2023, who is 14th in line to the throne.

15. Princess Eugenie’s third baby

Eugenie’s third child, a baby girl, who was born on Monday 3 August 2026, at 6.20pm, at a hospital in Lisbon, Portugal, is 15th in line to the throne.

16. Prince Edward, the Duke of Edinburgh

Following the Princesses of York and their children in succession is Prince Edward, 61, the Duke of Edinburgh, who is now 16th in line to the throne.

open image in gallery Prince Edward, 61, the Duke of Edinburgh ( Getty )

17. James Mountbatten-Windsor, Earl of Wessex

The 17th in line to the throne is Prince Edward’s youngest son, James, 18, who is also the Queen’s youngest grandchild.

18. The Lady Louise Mountbatten-Windsor

The Earl of Wessex is followed in the line of succession by his older sister, Louise, 22, who is 18th in line to the throne.

19. The Princess Royal

The Princess Royal, 75, also known as Princess Anne, is the 19th in line to the throne.

open image in gallery Princess Anne, is the 19th in line to the throne ( Getty )

20. Mr Peter Phillips

Princess Anne is followed in the line of succession by her son, Peter Philips, 48, who is 20th in line to the throne.

21. Miss Savannah Phillips

Savannah Phillips, 15, Peter’s eldest daughter, is 21st in line to the throne.

22. Miss Isla Phillips

Princess Anne’s youngest granddaughter, Isla Philips, 14, is 22nd in line to the throne.

23. Zara Tindall

The Queen’s eldest grandchild Zara Tindall, 45, the daughter of Princess Anne, is 23rd in line to the throne.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

News.title: Oil plummets as Trump calls off Iran strikes
News.content:
Oil prices have plunged after Donald Trump called off strikes and said the US and Iran would hold further peace talks.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, sank as much as 9.5pc early on Monday to less than $82 a barrel after the US president said he had halted plans for “disastrous” strikes.

Mr Trump said: “Obviously, they don’t want to be attacked. They knew the extent of the attack because they saw it forming.

“Now what we’re doing is we’re talking to them in the form of a negotiation. It begins tomorrow afternoon.”

Mr ‌Trump also ordered oil companies to lower petrol prices for American ‌consumers ‌and criticised ⁠Chevron’s chief executive for not crediting his administration for supporting the fossil fuel industry.

The president said that he had been asked by Iran as well as US partners Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar to hold off on strikes. He halted plans for a major attack against Iran on Saturday, which he said would have been the biggest since the Second World War.

Mr Trump claimed the sides were on the “perimeter” of a peace deal.

Oil’s sharp fall also sent the cost of government borrowing lower on Monday over hopes that it would ease inflation.

The yield on 10-year UK gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, dropped from 5.05pc to 4.98pc, while the equivalent US bonds dropped from 4.74pc to 4.69pc.

Stock markets in Europe also rose, with the FTSE 100 up 0.2pc, the Cac 40 in Paris up 0.3pc and the Dax in Frankfurt climbing 0.1pc.

News.title: Inside the trial for a vaccine to end malaria
News.content:
A small group of brave volunteers were given an experimental vaccine in Oxford this week in a bid to bring to an end the centuries-old scourge of malaria.

“I’m on my second vaccine now. Then I’m due to have my third vaccine soon, and then in November, I’ll be given malaria,” said an upbeat Mike Luciw, a 32-year-old local who works in recruitment.

“The hope is to help find something that could save millions of people.”

There are already two licenced vaccines for malaria but the new Oxford “RH5” shot is not like anything that has come before.

The existing jabs only act against malaria as it moves towards the liver in the early stage of infection, and provide only partial protection.

The new combination vaccine, in contrast, is designed to fight it off both at the liver stage and in the wider bloodstream, effectively knocking it out altogether.

The project is being run by the husband and wife team of Simon Draper, Professor of Vaccinology and Translational Medicine at the University of Oxford, and Professor Angela Minassian, an infectious disease specialist and clinical lead for their malaria programme in Oxford’s Department of Paediatrics.

“The dream for malaria … has been to have these two lines of defence, liver and blood, so if the first line fails, you’ve got a second,” says Prof Draper, who leads on the science.

“Our dream is to have a vaccine that gives over 90 per cent efficacy in African children,” adds Prof Minassian, who heads the clinical trials for the new jab.

News.title: Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage for this pre-season friendly between Girona and Arsenal at Estadi Montilivi in Catalonia.

With the transfer speculation surrounding Vinícius Júnior’s and Bruno Guimaraes’ potential moves to Arsenal ramping up, the reigning Premier League champions are in action against Girona as they step up their preparations ahead of the upcoming campaign.

Unlike other Premier League heavyweights, Arsenal have kept their pre-season tour relatively local with a selection of games in Spain, Ireland and England, before they face Manchester City in the FA Community Shield on August 16 at the Millennium Stadium in Cardiff.

Arsenal beat League One side MK Dons 3-0 in a behind-closed-doors friendly on July 25 at the Sobha Realty Training Centre, thanks to goals from Reiss Nelson, Ethan Nwaneri and Ceadach O’Neill.

After featuring in this victory and setting up Nelson for the opener, Christos Tzolis will be looking to continue his positive momentum with his new club, after joining Arsenal for £34m earlier this summer. Many fans will be keeping a close eye on the recently-signed winger given that various core members of last season’s Premier League-winning squad are yet to return from their post-World Cup breaks, having progressed deep in the competition.

Tournament winners David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, Norway captain Martin Odegaard, as well as England internationals Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke are all missing for this game, while France’s William Saliba is out injured and set for an extended period on the sidelines.

Those who exited the World Cup earlier than the aforementioned players, including Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Piero Hincapie, Kai Havertz, and Viktor Gyokeres, have all joined up with the squad in northern Spain.

Mikel Arteta’s men will play a wounded Girona, who suffered relegation from the top flight of Spanish football last season due to a 19th-place finish.

Kick-off is at 19:00, with team news arriving shortly.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford could get revenge in first match for Man Utd in nearly two years as he nears unlikely return
Sports.content:
MARCUS RASHFORD could mark his return to Manchester United in an awkward showdown against old foe Ruben Amorim.

The 28-year-old winger is set to report back for pre-season, alongside England teammate Kobbie Mainoo and World Cup runner-up Lisandro Martinez.



While United remain tight-lipped about Rashford’s exact timetable, his return will likely align with Mainoo and Martinez, who are both due back on Monday.

A three-week break following his final tournament match places him in the Republic of Ireland for next week’s training camp in Maynooth.



Should that happen, his first game could be against AC Milan, now managed by ex-United head coach Amorim, in Wroclaw on August 15.

It is unlikely that Carrick will play Rashford against Leeds at Croke Park next Wednesday with just a couple of days’ training behind him.



Rashford will almost certainly not be ‘bombed out’ again like he was under Amorim last summer.

Carrick is a calm character who is more pacifying than Amorim, having been a teammate of Rashford’s in 2016, coached him for years and managed him briefly for three interim games in 2021.

When Rashford’s season-long loan was unveiled by Barcelona last July, no-one expected to see the boyhood star back in a United shirt as Matheus Cunha swiped his No10 jersey.

Rashford’s Old Trafford future was dead and buried when Amorim was in charge after his final appearance against Viktoria Plzen in the Europa League on December 12.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Amorim had only been at United for a month when he became unhappy with the forward’s training standards, before dropping him and Alejandro Garnacho for the derby on December 15, which United won 2-1.

Amorim then famously said he would rather play his 63-year-old goalkeeper coach Jorge Vital than Rashford in January last year, days before the player joined Aston Villa on a six-month loan.

It’s just over a year to the day that Rashford scored his first goal for Barcelona in a pre-season win over Daegu in South Korea.

As it stands, the feeling at United and within Rashford’s camp is that he is likely to return this season.



His £325,000-a-week salary, agreed in 2023, is difficult to budge, which played a role in Barcelona failing to trigger the £26m option to buy clause.

Rashford is United’s highest earner again and has turned away offers because he is unwilling to take a pay cut.

Though his form dipped during his final two seasons at United, Carrick could revitalise Rashford just as he did Mainoo.

Like Mainoo, Rashford’s primary issue was with Amorim, while friction with other club figures may linger.

But there are no guarantees that Rashford will be a United player when the window closes next month, but the club are aware that any suitable replacement would cost a bomb.



Barca paid the entirety of his wages during the season on loan, but were only prepared to offer half the £26m price tag to make the move permanent.

United rejected any notion of another loan and Barca signed England pal Anthony Gordon for £70m from Newcastle and German winger Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

Once the deadline for Barca to sign Rashford expired on June 15, United disclosed that they would listen to offers of £40m from other clubs – with the exception of City and Liverpool – until that option ran out in mid-July.

He scored 11 goals and made 14 assists as Barca won the La Liga title, the Spanish Super Cup and reached the Champions League quarter-finals.

United have been in the market for a left-sided attacker and Rashford has the potential to be one of the best in the Prem – if his form can remain consistent.

Sports.title: Youth football star, 15, shot dead ‘after being mistaken for another target’ moments after playing in friendly
Sports.content:
TEENAGE TRAGEDY Youth football star, 15, shot dead ‘after being mistaken for another target’ moments after playing in friendly

A YOUNG Brazilian footballer with dreams of going pro has been shot dead ‘by mistake’.

Former Sao Paulo youth star Micael Leandro da Silva was just 15 years old when he was struck by a bullet in Maceio on Saturday.



Police believe the shooting was carried out by rival drug trafficking gangs and that Micael, with no known ties to criminal activity, was hit after being mistaken for another target.

The teenager was rushed to hospital but he died from his injuries.



Several other people were also struck during the attack.

Minutes before the shooting, Micael had been playing in an amateur football tournament.

His dad, Marcos Antonio Leandro, told local media: “My family has been torn apart by two criminals who came and shot my son in the back.

“The match had just finished and he was getting changed, so he had no chance to run.

“I’m devastated. His siblings haven’t stopped crying.

“I brought all my children up with humility, showing them how to be good people. It’s not easy to lose a son who had so many dreams.”



Micael left the Sao Paulo academy in April and spent time training with fourth-tier club Centro Sportivo Alagoano.

He was due to continue his youth football journey with lower league club Retro FC Brasil.

Dad Marcos, who was an amateur footballer himself, added: “From a very young age, he stood out in football. It was all he lived and breathed.

“He’d already won futsal and football titles with CSA. He was excited about getting back on the pitch and couldn’t wait for the days to pass so he could to join Retro.”

The 20-year-old’s stock rocketed during the World Cup after scoring the only goal as Ghana stunned Panama, with the winner brilliantly set up by Brandon Thomas-Asante.

Sports.title: Man Utd legend Mark Hughes’ son, 38, died from sudden adult death syndrome after collapsing in bedroom, inquest hears
Sports.content:
'TOTALLY HEARTBROKEN' Man Utd legend Mark Hughes’ son, 38, died from sudden adult death syndrome after collapsing in bedroom, inquest hears

THE son of Manchester United legend Mark Hughes died tragically from sudden adult death syndrome, an inquest heard.

Alex Hughes had been working in a top job in Grimsby Town‘s player recruitment department when he passed away aged 38.



It has now been revealed that Alex died after collapsing on the floor of his bedroom in his home, the inquest was told.

Thirty-eight-year-old player recruitment lead Alex was found by his two sons on June 19 at his £1.2m home in Prestbury, Cheshire at around 7am.



The inquest was told that Alex’s eldest son carried out CPR on his dad but he sadly died.

Cheshire Coroners Court was told that medics put down the cause of death to sudden adult death syndrome.

The hearing in Warrington heard that the condition usually occurs in young men and there are around 800 cases per year in England.

Area coroner Victoria Davies gave the cause of death as sudden adult death syndrome and also concluded that the death was down to natural causes.



Two-times Premier League winner Mark Hughes, 62, said his family was “totally heartbroken” by Alex’s sudden death on June 19.

Legendary football manager Sir Alex Ferguson led mourners as footballing figures packed into St Peter’s Church in Prestbury, Cheshire, to pay tribute last month.

United greats Bryan Robson and Ryan Giggs were in attendance, as well as ex-coach Mike Phelan and former chairman Martin Edwards.

Grimsby Town boss David Artell, who worked very closely with Alex during his time at the Mariners, also led a delegation from the League Two club.

Alex left behind his wife Jess – who he met at school when they were teenagers – and their children, Sebastian and Leonardo.



Born in 1987 while Mark was contracted to Barcelona, Alex went on to have a brief spell as a footballer in Wales.

He then moved into a variety of behind-the-scenes roles and earned his stripes as a match analyst at Blackburn.

Manchester City then took him on as a scout, going on to work as chief analyst at another of his dad’s former clubs, Fulham.

Alex later forged his own path with advisory roles at 1860 Munich and Reading.

In 2024, he took over as director of football at AFC Fylde before returning to prominent scouting roles at Morecambe and Grimsby.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Alex’s father Mark had a distinguished playing career with United, Barca, Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Southampton, Everton and Blackburn.

He then became a mainstay in Premier League management after five years in charge of the Welsh national team.

The recent French and European champion lit up the World Cup by leaving Theo Hernandez for dust and slamming a stunning solo goal for Senegal against France.

A fearless, technical dribbler with serious acceleration, Mbaye seems a perfect match for new Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola‘s high-intensity play style.

While attempts to bring Barcola to Merseyside have stalled over PSG’s eye-watering £145m price demands, Mbaye is believed to be valued at a more modest £34m.

Sports.title: How Roberto De Zerbi lured £52million star Paul van Hecke to Tottenham by telling him to ‘f*** off’
Sports.content:
ROBERTO DE ZERBI told Jan Paul van Hecke to “F*** off” to convince him to join Tottenham.

If that sounds an odd way to win over a target, or you are confused as to why new signings have snubbed bigger clubs for Spurs, spend a few minutes in his company and the clouds will part.



To borrow a phrase from another managerial great, the Italian is not one of the bottle. A nightmare to manage for owners? Probably. A delight for players? Absolutely.

Those who have worked with De Zerbi talk about him like some sort of demagog.



His fire, wit and undeniable emotional intelligence mean players are happy to look beyond bigger names or pay-cheques to work with him.

Sandro Tonali was courted by a host of top Premier League clubs while Mateus Fernandes turned down Manchester United to work with De Zerbi at Tottenham, who have finished 17th two years in a row.



Jan Paul van Hecke, who played under the Spurs boss at Brighton, had little choice.

But De Zerbi’s pursuit of the Dutchman says everything about his character.

The self-proclaimed ‘shark’ in the transfer market left it about an hour after Spurs secured survival to pin the defender, who had setup a goal against Tottenham weeks before.

De Zerbi said: “After the Everton game, I sent the message, ‘F* off, you wanted to push down Tottenham for Brighton when you made the assist to Giorginio Rutter. Now you have to come to me, yes or yes, you have no choice!’



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“After the game, right in my dressing room, my office in Tottenham stadium, I sent a message to my daughter, and then JP.

“I am excited when we close the deal, yes, but not for the player. We can play with JP, without JP, with Tonali, without Tonali, but it’s a different relationship, it’s a different atmosphere.

“If the coach calls the player, you can build a special connection at the beginning with the player, because the player knows you are the key for this transfer, and maybe this player feels to have to give you back something more than if Johan Lange call the player.

“You can create the special connection. With Mateus Fernandes, I spoke with the parents, with mum, with the father.”

De Zerbi, who excitedly beats the table, where his phone and cigarettes sit, throughout this hour-long tour de force, thumps his chest when he explains where the desire to be so close with his players comes from.



He added: “It’s in here. Because me as a player, as a student at school. When I felt the relationship with the teacher, with the coach, I was able to give my best.

“If I didn’t feel the connection, if I didn’t feel he appreciated me, the teacher, or a coach, I close myself, we start a war.

“It’s good, especially for the new generation. The young players, no? If they feel the coach loves me, the coach appreciates me, as a player, as a guy, they are in the right condition, in the better condition, to show who they are.”

An inability to show who they are, or how good they are, has been a chronic problem at Tottenham in the past two years.

As always, there was a characteristically De Zerbi answer to this problem. His first game of seven to save Spurs was a 1-0 defeat at Sunderland.



Walking into the away changing room at the Stadium of Light, he was staggered by what he found.

De Zerbi said: “I saw the players after Sunderland in the dressing room, I didn’t tell you in the press conference, but it was like this: all people cry, lying down on the floor in the dressing room.

“I said, ‘Did we pass away?’ I tried to transfer positivity and to observe the situation from another perspective.”

After gathering all the staff at Spurs’ Hotspur Way training ground and telling them to go home if they could not put on their best smile, there was a typically De Zerbi solution to lifting spirits within the squad – a night on the lash.

He added: “One big dinner in Bacchanalia in Mayfair, with alcohol.



“Alcohol is a good medicine. If you enjoy normally and seriously, not as stupid people. I believe in staying together.”

“Then, I transferred every day my opinion about them. They considered themselves in that moment worse than the people thought.”

De Zerbi hopes the players will now start organising their own nights out, and knows he is placing a lot of trust in them.

But this is a man who does not set rules. He is firm when needed, but wants his players to feel they can be themselves – so long as they give him everything while working.

He added: “[I ask for their] Testa, their head, and cervello, their brain, that’s it. All day.



“Football is based on every single day. Football is not like the light, you switch on one and then you switch off.

“There are the right moment to enjoy, for example, restaurants, they have to do what they want without rules.

“I don’t love rules. I read a book where it was written that creative people don’t follow any rules. I would like creative players.

I don’t want to set any rules. Just a couple, two or three at most. In terms of players of being together.

“I am not a policeman, not with my children. Freedom, totally freedom. One is one. You are like me, or like kit man, the same.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But every day we have to push, every day we have to deserve to stay here or to play football or to earn the money we earn. It’s not normal. We have to respect the luck we have had in our life.”

Anyone working at the top level in football has had some level of fortune, but while De Zerbi considers himself lucky to be at Tottenham – they can feel the same about having him.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino faces lengthy ban and disciplinary action as crisis meeting held today

A crisis meeting has been called as pressure continues to mount on FIFA president Gianni Infantino

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino's future as FIFA president is under serious threat (Image: Getty)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has summoned his top chiefs to a crunch crisis meeting today as he fights to save his job following the explosive fallout from his botched private equity deal. The embattled FIFA boss has called an emergency summit with senior leadership in Morocco in a desperate bid to shore up his position.

‌



It comes after he secretly hatched a highly controversial scheme to spin off the governing body's commercial operations into a new subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise.

‌



The project aimed to sell a 20 per cent stake in the commercial and tournament rights of the World Cup to private investors. Although a fierce global backlash and threats of a massive boycott from UEFA forced Infantino into a humiliating climbdown to scrap the proposal last week, furious football leaders insist the damage is done.

‌



While Infantino uses today's crisis talks in Rabat to try and stabilise his reign and cling to power, an outraged European football establishment is at open war with him and exploring two distinct legal avenues to force him out.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

The first option being discussed is triggering an emergency vote of no confidence. Under official FIFA statutes, an extraordinary Congress can be called if requested by at least 20 per cent of member associations - equating to 43 of FIFA's 211 global members.

‌



View 2 Images Infantino has called a crisis meeting as he scrambles to save his job (Image: Getty Images)

With UEFA alone boasting 55 member associations, European football easily clears that threshold on its own to force a congress within three months.

However, actually ousting Infantino at the meeting would still require a simple majority of all 211 global members, where every nation holds a single vote regardless of size.

‌



The second option - and a far more explosive route to remove Infantino - is through formal disciplinary action. FIFA's independent Ethics Committee has the authority to investigate alleged breaches of the FIFA Code of Ethics and hand down severe sanctions, including lengthy bans from all football-related activities.

This is the exact mechanism that brought down former president Sepp Blatter in 2015. Whilst no official ethics investigation has been opened yet, a lengthy ban remains the ultimate nuclear option to force him out immediately.

The next official presidential election is scheduled for March 18, 2027, with nominations closing on November 18. Infantino had previously been expected to win by a landslide but after pushing the game to the brink, he may find today's crisis summit marks the beginning of the end.

Sports.title: Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical
Sports.content:
Man Utd overhaul accelerates with another transfer agreed after booking medical

Manchester United are ready to sanction the exits of two goalkeepers in Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek having signed two this summer to back up Senne Lammens

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir is set for a move to La Liga

Manchester United continue to overhaul their goalkeeping ranks with Altay Bayindir set to depart for Spain and Radek Vitek on the verge of a move to the Championship.

‌



The situation between the sticks at Old Trafford has kept changing over the past three years with Senne Lammens establishing himself as the club's new No 1 last term. Underneath him players have left in search of more minutes, which has ultimately led Bayindir to head overseas.

‌



The Turkish goalkeeper spent the majority of his time at Old Trafford as a back-up, starting just six times in the Premier League last term, and a deal has now been agreed with Celta Vigo.

‌



He will join on a season-long loan with his wages covered by the La Liga side. Celta Vigo have the option to make the move permanent for £3.5million and it is understood United have a high sell-on clause attached in the deal.

Vitek, the 22-year-old Czech who impressed last season at Bristol City, is on his way back to the second tier as he prepares to join Middlesbrough, subject to a medical, in deal worth up to £14m. United retain a buy back option as well as a sell on clause that, Sky Sports claim, is a hefty 35 percent.

To cover for those departures United have signed Karl Darlow from Leeds after he became available on a free. He played 24 times for the Whites last term as they retained Premier League status. United also bought in teenage goalkeeper Kit Margetson from Swansea at the end of July.

‌



The moves continue to see United's goalkeeping landscape change. Lammens came in this time last year as an unknown quantity from Royal Antwerp but within months of arriving was promoted to become the team's first choice, keeping eight clean sheets as United finished third.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek is closing in on a move to Middlesbrough

His rise came after Andre Onana's surprise departure. The Cameroonian had endured a difficult time in Manchester having arrived from Inter Milan with an impressive reputation, but he continued to make notable errors that cost the team. He was allowed to leave on loan for Trabzonspor, who paid his wages in full.

‌



He has since returned to the Super Lig outfit for another year. Onana was ultimately signed by Erik ten Hag to replace David de Gea, who was allowed to leave on a free after spending more than a decade as the team's undisputed No 1.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah spotted in new shirt for first time as Liverpool icon mobbed after transfer
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah spotted in new shirt for first time as Liverpool icon mobbed after transfer

Mohamed Salah is joining a new club after weeks of speculation over his future having left Liverpool this summer following nine years at the club

View 2 Images Liverpool icon Mohamed Salah has landed in Turkey ahead of a move to Trabzonspor (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mohamed Salah has arrived in Istanbul wearing Trabzonspor's shirt, having agreed to join the Turkish side after leaving Liverpool at the end of last season. The 34-year-old will pen a two-year deal, according to reports.

‌



The Egyptian had been heavily linked with a move to Saudi Arabia but clubs in Turkey also pushed hard for his signature. Talks with Besiktas over a transfer took place last month, only for the move to break down.

‌



But it's now Trabzonspor who have won the race for his signature, with the club announcing they were in transfer talks with Salah on Tuesday night and that he would arrive in Trabzon on Wednesday.

‌



Virgil van Dijk transfer lined up as club chiefs 'gutted' at missed Liverpool opportunity READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola offer delay explained as PSG clear way with medical booked READ MORE :

They stated: "Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5. The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

"The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club’s official communication channels during the day."

Salah was greeted by several journalists outside of the airport as well as fans.

‌



Salah will link up with Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana, who has returned to the club on loan for a second season. Former Manchester City defender Stefan Savic is another ex‑Premier League player currently plying his trade with the Super Lig side.

View 2 Images Mohamed Salah pictured in a Trabzonspor shirt (Image: Cemal Yurttas/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Salah bid an emotional farewell when his plan to exit the Reds was announced in March. ""Liverpool is not just a football club, it's a passion, it's a history, it's a spirit," he said. "I can't explain in words to anyone not part of this club.

Article continues below

"We celebrated victory, we won the most important trophies and we fought together through the hardest time in our life.

"I want to thank everyone who was part of this club throughout my time here, especially the teammates past and present.

"And to the fans, I don't have enough words. The support you showed me through the best time of my career and you stood by me in the toughest times. It's something I will never forget and something I will take with me always."

Sports.title: How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer
Sports.content:
How Arsenal could line up after signing Bruno Guimaraes and completing Vinicius Jr transfer

Arsenal are closing on their first major signing of the summer in Bruno Guimaraes whilst they're tracking Vinicius Junior's situation as the Premier League champions seek to add more quality

View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes is set to swap Newcastle for Arsenal (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

Arsenal are closing in on the signing of Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle as they look to land their biggest coup of the summer so far.

‌



The Premier League champions are already favourites to defend their title and have gone after proven talent with the Brazilian set to move for £75million. It became clear weeks ago that Guimaraes wanted out of St James' Park and had cited Arsenal as his ideal destination.

‌



Bolstering midfield was not necessarily a priority at the Emirates, but when a player of his quality became available a swoop was always on the cards. Declan Rice is the only guaranteed starter in the Arsenal midfield, leaving Mikel Arteta to fit pieces of the jigsaw around him.

‌



Guimaraes has been the driving force behind Newcastle's rise - and the club were linked with him when he moved to England from Lyon back in 2022.

The 29-year-old will battle with the likes of Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi for a starting role, whilst Arsenal could equally look to play with a flat three, as opposed to two sitting and one playmaker. Zubimendi and Guimaraes have shown themselves more than capable of picking passes between the lines and stretching defences.

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

One man who may well suffer a knock-on effect should Guimaraes head south is Martin Odegaard. Once the team's unchallenged playmaker, the Norwegian has seen more and more individuals join who can challenge him for his spot. He was injured for periods last term but he may not enjoy the untouchable status he once did.

‌



Arsenal, in the wake of their Champions League final loss, where they were dominated from a footballing point of view, were urged to add more quality in the final third.

They could yet bring in one of the world's best as they continue to track Vinicius Junior's situation at Real Madrid. The winger is about to enter the final year of his contract at the Bernabeu and Los Blancos want to avoid losing him for nothing.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is locked in a contract standoff with Real Madrid (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



Their negotiations centre on the player's image rights and where he sits in the financial pecking order. Vinicius wants to earn the same as Kylian Mbappe, Real's top earner, but the club are reluctant to do so - and Arsenal could yet swoop in as reports claim they would make him the Premier League's highest-ever earner.

That would see him pocket weekly wages that are north of £500,000-a-week. Such an investment would see Vinicius go straight in on Arsenal's left side with Bukayo Saka still the team's main man on the right, even if his form has dropped off over the last 12 months.

The central figure of their attack remains an issue, despite the £64m investment they made in Viktor Gyokeres last summer. The Swede scored 20 times in his debut season but question marks remain and he was ultimately left out for the Champions League final against PSG.

‌



Kai Havertz, who scored that night in Budapest, was picked instead and whilst the German links play better than anyone in the Arsenal side, his lack of goals have been cited as an issue when compared to some of Europe's heavyweights. It leaves Arteta with a decision on who to back - or whether to dip back into the market.

View 3 Images Arsenal would likely have to shell out £200m in order to land Bruno Guimaraes and Vinicius Jnr

Arsenal's frontline is already heavily congested with Noni Madueke, Gabriel Martinelli, Eberechi Eze, new signing Christos Tzolis and academy graduate Ethan Nwaneri all eyeing minutes. The latter was forced to head out on loan last term after being continually overlooked.

‌



Defensively Arsenal remain one of Europe's best - if not the best. Their world class centre-half pairing of Gabriel and William Saliba has been the cornerstone of their rise in recent years, although the Frenchman will spend a period on the sidelines, leaving someone to fill the void initially.

Piero Hincapie was signed permanently this summer and has impressed at left-back whilst Jurrien Timber, when fit, is perhaps the most versatile defender in the team and equally impressive at centre-half or on either flank.

David Raya, off the back of having to accept not being Spain's No 1, continues to prove himself as one of the world's best for Arsenal. The club have signed Illan Meslier to serve as a back-up option.

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr is a game-changing transfer that even non-Arsenal fans should want done
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr is a game-changing transfer that even non-Arsenal fans should want done

Arsenal have managed to tempt Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle and the Premier League champions are still hopeful of bringing Real Madrid's star attacker to the Premier League

View 3 Images Vinicius Junior is having make-or-break contract talks with Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Bruno Guimaraes is a solid, high-end signing for Arsenal but it is not a game-changing transfer. At Newcastle United, the Brazilian has proven himself to be a very effective performer in the context of the Premier League’s particular demands.

‌



For a start, he covers a lot of ground. In a 4-3 win over Leeds United at St James’ Park in January of this year, Guimaraes ran 13.24km - that is well over eight miles. Only two other players broke the 13km mark in a single Premier League game last season. Manchester City’s Bernardo Silva did it against Nottingham Forest and Brighton’s Pascal Gross did it twice, against City and Chelsea.

‌



Guimaraes is a committed character, that is for sure. It is probably fair to say he was the heartbeat of the Eddie Howe team that ended Newcastle’s long wait for a major trophy and qualified for two Champions League campaigns.

‌



In those Champions League campaigns, Guimaraes featured in 13 matches, failed to score and produced only one assist. His Premier League numbers are significantly better, scoring 30 times (two of which were penalties) for Newcastle and contributing 26 assists.

More detailed statistics show Guimaraes has, across the last three seasons, won more duels (697) than any other Premier League player. Mikel Arteta, in common with most Premier League managers, loves a player who can win a duel.

And judging by the prices in most top-level midfield transactions this summer, a fee in the region of £75million for the 28-year-old is a relatively reasonable figure. But he is not a game-changer. His countryman Vinicius Junior most certainly is.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Guimaraes will soon complete his £75million to Arsenal (Image: Getty)

Vinicius Junior and his advisers are scheduled to meet with Real Madrid executives any time now for what are being seen as make-or-break talks over his contract impasse. The 26-year-old attacker has a year left on his deal and wants a £10million-a-year increase to his current salary of £15million.

Real’s offer stands at an annual £19mllion - still £6million shy. Arsenal would have to shatter any sort of pay-scale they have but this would be a one-off move.

‌



This would be a statement signing of the highest order. For all the Premier League’s self-proclamation about being the best club competition in the world, it still struggles to attract the ultimate marquee players.

They normally go to Real Madrid, not leave Real Madrid. Vinicius Junior has been a flagship player at the Bernabeu and, most significantly, a proven Champions League performer.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr would give Mikel Arteta that extra attacking dimension he needs (Image: DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal and Arteta deserved great credit for going all the way to the final - and to a penalty shootout - last season but they lacked just one extra, attacking dimension. Vinicius Junior would provide that.

He has 26 goals and 21 assists in his last 46 Champions League appearances. And while Arsenal fans will rightfully dismiss it as unimportant, Vinicius Junior will make them more watchable. He will make the Premier League more watchable.

Clearly, there is still a lot of work to be done if Arsenal are to tempt Vinicius Junior to the Emirates. But even you are not a Gunner, it is a move that the Premier League should be desperate for.

Sports.title: Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan
Sports.content:
Arsenal 'already plotting' next signing after Bruno Guimaraes swoop and Vinicius Jr plan

Arsenal have agreed a deal with Newcastle United for Bruno Guimaraes and have their eyes set on their next summer signing

View 2 Images Arsenal are closing in on Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal have reportedly set their sights on a new central defender this summer as they look for cover after William Saliba aggravated a back injury on international duty at the World Cup. The Gunners are closing in on the £75million signing of Bruno Guimaraes and are exploring a blockbuster deal for Vinicius Junior, but a new defender is also being targeted.

‌



Saliba was replaced in France's semi-final defeat to Spain after going down injured, with new Chelsea signing Mazence Lacroix brought on as his replacement.

‌



Head coach Didier Deschamps did not risk Saliba during the third-placed play-off against England, though he did name the Arsenal defender on the substitutes' bench. Arsenal released a medical update four days later following Saliba's return to London from the United States.

‌



The club confirmed he is expected to miss part of the new season and will be sidelined for a prolonged spell as he undertakes a managed recovery programme. Now, according toFabrizio Romano, the Gunners will bring in a new defender to cover for Saliba.

Alan Brazil gives health update as radio legend returns to air after life-saving operation READ MORE :

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Deschamps revealed ahead of France's final game that Saliba had been managing the injury since March. He said: "William Saliba got injured, and it's problematic. He went through some examinations, and the injury did not worsen. He has faced that injury since March; he had some pain, and unfortunately, the pain was not bearable".

‌



Arsenal, however, maintain that thorough assessments have determined that surgery is not required. Specialist evaluations established that the injury would necessitate a period of rehabilitation instead.

Back troubles previously affected Saliba three years ago. His 2022/23 season was brought to an end prematurely after injuring his back during the second leg of Arsenal's Europa League last-16 encounter against Sporting.

He was sidelined for the final 11 Premier League matches and missed four of France's European Championship qualifiers as well. Saliba made his comeback four months afterwards during Arsenal's pre-season programme.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta will be without William Saliba for the start of the new season (Image: ANTONIN THUILLIER, AFP via Getty Images)

The club have brought in defenders Cristhian Mosquera, Jurrien Timber, Piero Hincapie and Riccardo Calafiori since that period, but may have to bring in further defensive reinforcements. This summer, the former has featured as a right-sided centre half, partnering Gabriel against Girona, with boss Mikel Arteta evidently grooming him to deputise for Saliba.

Ben White represents another alternative who can shift infield from right-back to operate centrally. Arsenal, though, continue to monitor the market for cover.

‌



England international Ezri Konsa was said to be under consideration, but Aston Villa's asking price in excess of £50m hampers any prospective transfer. Former Man City defender John Stones was also considered before joining Inter on a free transfer, while Arsenal have also been linked with other defenders.

Arsenal are on the brink of landing a statement signing regarding Guimaraes, after agreeing a £75m deal with Newcastle United for their captain.

The Gunners are also hopeful of pulling off one of the transfers of the summer by signing Real Madrid star Vinicius Jr, who is in the final 12 months of his contract at the Bernabeu.

Sports.title: Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request
Sports.content:
Inside the murky world of FIFA lobbying as Jamie Carragher reveals World Cup request

The former Liverpool captain has shed light on a private meeting he attended with FIFA officials and ex‑players to discuss proposals to play the World Cup every two years

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher says he was asked to support a new World Cup proposal (Image: YouTube / Football Ramble)

Jamie Carragher turned down FIFA's request to publicly support the idea of holding the World Cup every two years rather than the traditional four, following a secret meeting. The Sky Sports pundit revealed he had spoken with former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, now FIFA's chief of global football development, as well as a number of ex‑players about the proposed overhaul.

‌



This summer's tournament was staged across the United States, Canada and Mexico, with European champions Spain lifting the trophy for the first time in 16 years. Luis de la Fuente's side beat Argentina 1-0 in the final at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal.

‌



The next World Cup is scheduled for 2030, with Morocco, Portugal and holders Spain set to jointly host the tournament. However, former Liverpool defender Carragher has revealed that discussions have already taken place about shifting the competition to a more regular cycle.

‌



Arsene Wenger forced to break silence on Gianni Infantino's disastrous World Cup plan READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino calls FIFA crisis meeting in desperate attempt to cling to power READ MORE :

Speaking on the Football Ramble podcast, Carragher said he had taken part in discussions about the idea but didn't want to take it further. He admitted he was stunned when the organiser later messaged him asking him to publicly back the plan - a request he rejected immediately.

Carragher said: "I had a little chat with Arsene Wenger. He was getting involved with FIFA and it was all around this World Cup being every two years. He said, 'I'd like you to come on this other call with other ex players and we're going to chat about the ideas going forward'. I'm like, 'Brilliant, amazing'.

"We get on this Zoom and it wasn't just English players. It was like [Javier] Mascherano, there were foreign players from all over the world. They're basically talking about the pros of a World Cup every two years. I'm just listening, asking questions. I don't like the idea.

‌



"We finish this Zoom. I haven't said whether I don't like it or it shouldn't happen, I'm just chatting with these ex players. And the guy who was organising the Zoom, then text me and said, 'Okay, can you put this out?' - like supporting it. I was like, 'No, no, no'.

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger is FIFA's chief of global football development (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"Just because I came on the Zoom... I don't agree with and I don't want it. I think it's rubbish. This feeling of 'Once you're in here with us and you're on this Zoom, we're all these ex players and we're in.

"That was my insight into it with Wenger and Infantino above him, with getting all these ex players in and like, 'This makes us look okay'. Half of these ex players, they don't care. From that, I was like, 'I'm not having this at all'."

Plans for the proposal have not gathered momentum, though changes to the tournament were introduced for the first time this summer, with the 2026 edition expanding to 48 teams and adding an extra knockout round.

‌



Further reports suggest FIFA are considering pushing that even further, with a potential increase to 64 teams by the time the 2030 showpiece - the 100th anniversary of the World Cup arrives.

Both UEFA and CONCACAF oppose the idea, but CONMEBOL president Alejandro Dominguez remains firmly in favour. The 2030 World Cup, co‑hosted by Morocco, Portugal and Spain, will also stage matches in Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to mark the centenary.
