Sports.title: Football legend LUIS FIGO: Infantino's behaviour is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested I've ever seen. Nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends and he must go NOW
Sports.content:
Football legend LUIS FIGO: Infantino's behaviour is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested I've ever seen. Nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends and he must go NOW

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

I could write 10,000 words on the problems at FIFA. But the solution needs only three: Infantino must go.

I have loved football all my life. I was a professional player for 20 years. And believe me, I have met some rogues in my time in the game.

But what I have seen exposed in the last 10 days is the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested behaviour I have ever witnessed.

The man who would do that - the man who would try to force through such major changes just to enrich himself and his friends - is a relic of the game’s past and should have no part in its future.

If it was such a good idea, why not tell your members when you had them all in a room before the World Cup Final?

If it was such a robust plan, why not tell your members the risks as well as what you describe as the benefits?

Portugal legend Luis Figo (right) pictured with under pressure FIFA president Gianni Infantino

Infantino is holding crisis talks with staff after calling an urgent meeting in Morocco tomorrow

If the scheme was a no-brainer, why not be honest about the fact that it was going to give you a $30m-a-year job at the end of it?

But none of this was done. Because it’s not a good idea. It’s not robust when you fail to be transparent about the crippling returns that private equity always seek.

It’s not bold when you fail to explain that once you have sold your share it is gone forever and you have disinherited your successors from ownership of the World Cup.

And it’s not honest when you fail to mention that, after you have delivered the head of the World Cup on a platter to your mates in DC, they are going to give you a job worth five times your current salary.

None of this comes as a surprise when you consider the litany of abuses he has inflicted on football’s reputation; from suspending and reversing disciplinary decisions to breaking the laws of the game over a half-time show, nothing gets in the way of pleasing his friends.

Nor is it a surprise when you read the comments of (Jordan FA president) Prince Ali, highlighting the mob-like behaviour of Infantino’s FIFA; obstructing his FA’s work and funding in order to secure a nomination letter so that the reign of terrible self-interest can continue.

Football does need a discussion about money. But not the money that could go out of the game to investors or on bloated administrator salaries.

I mean the money that should be spent on building pitches and training coaches to make sure that every child in the world has the chance to fall in love with the most beautiful sport on the planet.

I mean the $5bn in FIFA’s reserves for a start. How many shares could that buy in this grubby, underhand plot? All of them! So there is no need for outside investment after all.

The FIFA president 'deviously' and 'cravenly' plotted to sell the World Cup to private investors

This plan – like the Super League before it – was blown apart by the media exposing every devious twist and turn before its advocates had their messaging straight. And thank goodness it was.

Infantino has debased the office of FIFA President that he promised to elevate. He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.

He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the FIFA Peace Prize winner.

It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now.

Luis Figo played almost 800 games in a glittering club career spanning Sporting Lisbon, Barcelona, Real Madrid and Inter Milan. He also won 127 caps for Portugal and has been a UEFA football advisor since 2017.

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi reveals the boozy dinner that saved Tottenham's season, why he's revelling in this transfer window... and his unorthodox, foul-mouthed pitch to persuade Jan Paul van Hecke to sign!
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi was in his office at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium after the final game of last season, a 1-0 victory over Everton which ensured they remained a Premier League club.

De Zerbi’s work for the day was not done. He had transfer targets for pursuing, such as Jan Paul van Hecke at Brighton, and so he began typing a text message to his former player.

‘With JP, after the Everton game, I sent the message, “F*** off. You wanted to push down Tottenham for Brighton when you made the assist to Georginio Rutter. Now you have to come to me. Yes or yes? You have no choice,”’ De Zerbi tells us.

‘After the game, right in my dressing room, in my office in the Tottenham stadium, I sent a message to my daughter, and then JP.’

Van Hecke had assisted Rutter for Brighton’s stoppage-time equaliser at Tottenham in April, a 2-2 draw which left De Zerbi with only five remaining fixtures to avoid relegation.

Daily Mail Sport were given time with Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi in Sydney

De Zerbi explained how he spoke to his former Brighton player Jan Paul van Hecke just hours after the final game of last season

Spurs survived, and now, they have signed Van Hecke from Brighton for £52million, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle for £100million, and Mateus Fernandes from West Ham for £85million, while also bringing in Andy Robertson and Marcos Senesi for free from Liverpool and Bournemouth respectively. De Zerbi tells us he isn’t finished yet, describing their summer as ‘60 per cent’ complete.

Spend some time with De Zerbi and you soon understand why so many big names are agreeing to sign up to the Spurs reboot. Daily Mail Sport was fortunate enough to have more than an hour in his company, inside a temporary boardroom set up at the chic InterContinental Hotel in Australia, within walking distance of the Sydney Opera House.

Most managers loathe the transfer window but not this ‘shark’, as De Zerbi describes himself.

‘If the coach calls the player, you can build a special connection at the beginning with the player, because the player knows you are the key for this transfer, and maybe this player feels to have to give you back something more than if Johan Lange (sporting director) calls the player,’ he says on transfers. ‘With Mateus Fernandes, I spoke with the parents, with his mum, with the father.

‘The most important thing about my job is the relationship I have as a man. Without that relationship I am not able to work. Without the relationship you can’t play good football and have a good style of play. It is 20 per cent coach, 80 per cent the person.

‘The facts are clear. Now we have to bring in top players to become competitive. I don't know if to win, but for sure to be better, and better than the last two seasons' results in the Premier League.

‘Robertson, I think, is a winner. JP, maybe you don't know, but he's a winner, a leader. Tonali is a winner. What do you think? I fought to bring in players ready to win or not?'

De Zerbi’s assistant, Enrico Venturelli, a lovely chap, is here with him for this interview, just in case he needs a little help with his English. On how he has found working with Tottenham’s higher-ups, De Zerbi continues: ‘It's my best connection with the board. Also in the players we sold. For (Luka) Vuskovic, it was together. The request of Vuskovic (to leave), we spoke with Vinai (Venkatesham, chief executive), with Johan, together, because the money of my club, I consider my money.

'It’s like the owner is my father. You don't want to ask your father to spend money or to lose money, and if we bring in a player, if we sell a player, it's one family. OK, we are spending money, but we are spending money for the plan, for the project.

‘The top clubs now, they are not worried about selling players. No. Even Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich, when they have to sell, they have to sell. Right price. You don't have to be shy. But when you have to spend money, you have to do that. Strong, fast, quickly, the right player, the right investment.’

The Italian boss recalled his big speech after Tottenham's defeat to Sunderland in April, which led to their resurgence and eventually survival

Tottenham have acted decisively after two successive 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League. De Zerbi insists he would have stayed even if Spurs had dropped down, and it was a real possibility. They lost their first league game under the 47-year-old Italian – 1-0 away at Sunderland.

‘I saw the players after Sunderland in the dressing room,’ De Zerbi recalls. ‘I didn’t tell you in the press conference, but it was like this: all people crying, lying down on the floor in the dressing room. I said, “We pass away?” and I tried to transfer positivity and to observe the situation from another perspective. I was honest. People inside the training ground were sad and negative.

‘The first day after Sunderland, I organised a meeting without the players (just staff) and I said, “The first one I see say something negative, I will send you home immediately. I don’t want to see anyone sad, negative, crying. If you stay positive, I give you my word we will stay together here.” It’s another crucial part, because the players live with these people.’

Asked what he did to pick up his broken players after Sunderland, De Zerbi reveals: ‘One big dinner in Bacchanalia in Mayfair – with alcohol. Alcohol is a good medicine. If you enjoy normally and seriously. Not as stupid people. I believe in staying together.

‘Then, I transferred every day my opinion about them. I think they considered themselves in that moment worse than people thought. There was the possibility to stay up and to win. In sport, between the players and the coach, if you have respect and values, it’s much better, and with love, friendship, care, you become top, top, top. Respect is normal. If I believe in you, it’s much better. But if I love you, you become unbelievable.’

Antonin Kinsky is among those set to benefit from De Zerbi’s show of trust, with the Spurs boss confirming when asked that he will be his first-choice goalkeeper next season. This follows the humiliation of Kinsky when Igor Tudor substituted him when 3-0 down after 17 minutes at Atletico Madrid. Kinsky was the best player when Spurs beat Chelsea 2-1 in their pre-season friendly in Sydney.

‘Me as a player, as a student at school, when I felt the relationship with the teacher, with the coach, I gave my best,’ De Zerbi says. ‘If I didn't feel the connection, if I didn't feel he appreciated me, the teacher or the coach, I close myself, we start a war.'

Upon taking over at Tottenham, De Zerbi says he held ‘one million’ individual meetings, some with players who may have been interested in leaving this summer. He tells us his message to them was: 'Help me stay up, then I will help you to leave. If you don't help me stay up, then you stay underwater with me.’ He praises Cristian Romero’s response, saying he was ‘unbelievable’, and while the Spurs captain could yet leave, he would do so with thanks from De Zerbi.

His message to others such as Djed Spence and Lucas Bergvall was: ‘I would like you stay if you want to stay. If you don't want to stay, if you want to leave, you have to leave. If you want to leave, speak with Vinai and Johan. Because I don't manage the price, the sale. I can speak with Vinai and Johan about the best strategy to do, but I don't decide £30m, £40m, that's not my position and I don't want to change my position. It's tough enough to be a coach and I want to stay as a coach.’

De Zerbi values his relationship with individual players and wants them to feel a connection with him

De Zerbi insists he should not be seen as a disciplinarian. ‘They have to do what they want without rules,’ he adds. ‘I don't love rules. I read a book where it was written that creative people don't follow rules. I would like creative players. I don't want to set any rules.

‘Just a couple, two or three at most, in terms of players being together. I am not a policeman. Not with my children. Freedom. Total freedom. One is one. Every day we have to push. Every day we have to deserve to stay here or to play football or to earn our money. It's not normal. We have to respect the luck we have had in our lives.’

What if someone betrays this show of trust? ‘What do you want to know? If I punch the player? Nothing, but I know to be stronger when I have to do something.’

De Zerbi is flattered that several coaches, such as Pep Guardiola and Enzo Maresca, have expressed their admiration for his work. ‘I become shy,’ he says. ‘I am not used to that and I don't think I will ever get used to it. We are lucky because we started from the s*** of football.’

De Zerbi has earned this opportunity to lead this reset for Tottenham, who remain one of the Premier League’s biggest clubs despite two struggling seasons. After an hour, we shake hands and go our separate ways – us understanding why so many footballers are in love with this manager, and him itching to get back to work.

Sports.title: Mohamed Salah closes on Turkey move: Former Liverpool star pictured in Trabzonspor kit and sends message to fans - as supporters gather at the airport ahead of his arrival
Sports.content:
Mohamed Salah was greeted by crowds of Trabzonspor fans after arriving in Istanbul ahead of completing a move to the Turkish club.

Fans had gathered in anticipation for Salah's arrival after the former Liverpool star travelled to the city on a private jet.

Salah was pictured on the jet wearing a Trabzonspor shirt, featuring his name and the number 61 - which is regularly used as a symbol of the city and the club.

A video was released by the club with Salah addressing fans ahead of his imminent arrival.

'Trabzon are you ready, I can hear you,' Salah said. 'See you very soon.'

The pictures and video were released as the 34-year-old began travelling from the Greek island of Mykonos, where he has been on holiday following his World Cup involvement with Egypt.

Bordo-Mavili formasıyla ilk kez kameraların karşısında… İlk mesajı Büyük Trabzonspor Taraftarına:



“Bize Her Yer Trabzon!” ❤️💙#SalahIsComing pic.twitter.com/Sr1KcRDwpk — Trabzonspor (@Trabzonspor) August 5, 2026

Mohamed Salah was greeted by Trabzonspor fans at the Ataturk Airport as he closes on a move to the Turkish side

Salah was seen conducting the crowds that had gathered ahead of his high-profile transfer

🔴🔵 Trabzonsporlu taraftarlar, Atatürk Havalimanı Genel Havacılık Terminali'nde Muhammed Salah'ı bekliyor. 📽️ pic.twitter.com/HhiszHpHXg — AA SPOR (@aa_spor) August 5, 2026

His club future is now close to being decided, having become a free agent after agreeing to tear up the final year of his Liverpool contract.

Trabzonspor had invited their supporters to pay to join a live stream following Salah's flight to Turkey, as fans gathered outside the Ataturk Airport ahead of his arrival.

A private jet took off from Mykonos Airport around 10.30am as Salah began his journey.

Turkish giants Besiktas were understood to be the Egyptian's first choice but talks with them stalled last week.

Trabzonspor revealed their talks with Salah on Tuesday night, with the club informing their 1.9million followers on X of his travel arrangements, as well as telling fans a welcome programme would be in place.

The club wrote: 'Public Announcement: Negotiations have begun regarding the transfer of professional footballer Mohamed Salah to our Club.'

The club then posted: 'Professional footballer Mohamed Salah, with whom we have begun transfer negotiations, will be at Istanbul Atatürk Airport General Aviation Terminal at 12:00 on Wednesday, August 5.

'The player is scheduled to arrive in Trabzon on the same day in the evening hours.

Salah had earlier been pictured on a private jet as he travelled from Mykonos to Istanbul

The former Liverpool star is set to sign a two-year contract with the Turkish club

Fans had arrived at the airport after Trabzonspor announced Salah's travel schedule for the day

Salah is set to continue his journey to Trabzon later today to complete the transfer

Trabzonspor fans celebrated the high-profile arrival of Salah ahead of the new season

'The time and other details regarding the welcome program in Trabzon will be shared with the public through our club's official communication channels during the day.'

Trabzonspor also shared a 17-second AI video of a camera shot panning from pyramids over mountains to a view of their 41,000-seater stadium Papara Park.

Salah's future has been the subject of huge interest since the surprising decision was announced back in March that he would leave Liverpool one year into his two-year contract extension.

Many anticipated that Saudi Arabia would be the most likely destination after Al-Ittihad made a £150million bid in summer 2023.

But Trabzonspor are now set to sign the winger, who fell out with Arne Slot at Anfield last term.

The Turkish side finished third last season behind Fenerbahce and champions Galatasaray.

Salah, who is the third-highest goalscorer in Reds history with 255, did not engage in talks with teams before the end of the season out of respect to the Merseyside club.

His long-serving agent, Ramy Abbas, repeatedly insisted nothing had been decided and reaffirmed that stance during the World Cup.

But since returning from the competition in the US, talks have accelerated with interested parties.

A Trabzonspor fan was seen kissing a tifo of Saah after his arrival at Istanbul airport

Salah is renowned for his remarkable professionalism and will back himself to remain at a high level deep into his thirties.

Salah was the star man as Slot’s side won the Premier League in Slot's first season, the Egyptian's second English title, but his level dipped last term with just ten goals compared to a staggering 34 when he spear-headed the 2024-25 title win.

Liverpool are yet to replace the player who was voted Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Players' Player of the Year three times at the club.

With the start of the season fast approaching, Bradley Barcola of PSG remains the most likely high-profile attacking signing.

But the 23-year-old, valued at £145million by his club, plays predominantly on the left and Jamie Carragher recently warned against buying him as a replacement for Salah.

Salah would be the most high-profile signing in Trabzonspor's history and if his expected move is confirmed, will join Man United loanee Andre Onana.

Ex-Man City defender Stefan Savic also plays for the Turkish side, who have won their domestic title seven times.

Sports.title: Manchester United star and former Wales manager Mark Hughes' son died of sudden adult death syndrome after being found by his children, inquest
Sports.content:
The son of Manchester United striker and former Wales manager Mark Hughes died tragically from sudden adult death syndrome, an inquest has found.

Alex Hughes, 38, collapsed on the floor of his bedroom where he was found by his two sons at 7am on June 19, a coroner was told.

Mr Hughes' oldest son, Sebastian, 11, carried out CPR but his father, the head of player recruitment at League Two Grimsby Town FC, could not be revived, the inquest heard.

Cheshire Coroner's Court heard the cause of death was found to be Sudden Adult Death Syndrome (SADS).

Today's hearing in Warrington heard that the condition usually occurs in young men and there are around 800 cases per year in England.

Area coroner Victoria Davies gave the cause of death as sudden adult death syndrome and concluded that the death was down to natural causes.

She said: 'A post mortem report showed there was no signification result of toxicology. There was no alcohol or drugs or prescription drugs.

'A cardiac pathology report showed sudden death with a normal heart.

'There were no other significant findings.

'SADS deaths occur predominantly in young males. There were are around 800 cases per annum in England.'

Mr Hughes' Manchester United legend father had announced the tragedy in an emotional statement, saying it had left his family 'totally heartbroken'.

Alex Hughes, 38, was head of player recruitment at League Two Grimsby Town FC

The former Wales, Blackburn, Manchester City and Stoke City boss carried his son's coffin at the funeral last month as he paid his final respects.

In a statement via the League Managers Association at the time of his son's death, Mr Hughes senior said: 'Jill and I are totally heartbroken by the sudden and unexpected loss of our beloved son Alex.

'Alex was a wonderful son, brother to Curtis and Xenna, devoted husband and father to Jessica and their two beautiful children Sebastian and Leonardo.

'Alex was Player Recruitment Lead at Grimsby Town FC, and had many good friends and colleagues.

'He will be so deeply missed by us all.'

Leading sports figures joined mourners for the funeral at St Peter's Church in Prestbury, Cheshire, last month.

Mr Hughes' wife Jess, whom he had known since school, was accompanied by their sons, Sebastian, 11, and Leonardo, 9.

Former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson attended the funeral along with stars including Bryan Robson and Ryan Giggs.

Mr Hughes' father Mark was among pallbearers at the father-of-two's funeral last month

Mr Hughes's father-in-law, David Pollock, gave a moving eulogy, explaining how he was proud of his boys, who had begun pointing to the skies after scoring goals.

Born in 1987, while his dad was contracted to Barcelona, Mr Hughes had a brief football career in Wales before moving into a variety of behind-the-scenes roles.

He earned his stripes as a match analyst at Blackburn before Man City took him on as a scout.

Mr Hughes, who lived at a £1.2m home in Prestbury, then worked as chief analyst at another of his dad’s former clubs, Fulham, before forging his own path with advisory roles at 1860 Munich and Reading.

In 2024 he took over as director of football at AFC Fylde before returning to prominent scouting roles at Morecambe and Grimsby.

Dad Mark Hughes, now 62, had a distinguished playing career with United, including helping win their first two Premier League titles in 1993 and 1994, Barca, Bayern Munich, Chelsea, Southampton, Everton and Blackburn.

He then became a mainstay in club management after five years in charge of the Welsh national team between 1999 and 2004.

Hughes was most recently in charge of Carlisle United but left after suffering defeat in the National League play-off semi-finals last season.

Coventry aim to break transfer record AGAIN

Coventry are attempting to break their transfer record for the second time this week after offering nearly £26million for Ghana star Caleb Yirenkyi.

The midfielder, who plays for Danish club Nordsjaelland, represented his country at this summer’s World Cup as they drew 0-0 with England and exited at the first knockout stage.

Back in the top flight for the first time in 25 years, the Sky Blues have already signed goalkeeper Carl Rushworth for £22.5m as well as defender Aurele Amenda and winger Loum Tchaouna. They have also turned on-loan midfielder Frank Onyeka’s move from Brentford into a permanent switch.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham responds to swimmer Archie Goodburn after Commonwealth Games star broke down on BBC Breakfast in heartfelt plea for brain cancer funding as he battles incurable diagnosis
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has invited British swimmer Archie Goodburn to a personal meeting after the Commonwealth Games star broke down in tears while making an emotional plea for more cancer research funding on BBC Breakfast yesterday.

The 25-year-old swimmer, who was diagnosed with inoperable brain tumours when he was just 22, implored the Prime Minister to invest more money and resources into cancer research by tearfully asking him to 'give us a chance to fight for our lives'.

Burnham, replying to a video of Goodburn's impassioned plea on TikTok, said: 'Archie, thank you for this. I know how hard it must have been.

'What you're doing for other people while you're going through all this yourself shows the best of us.

'I'd really like to meet you and hear from you directly and I've asked my team to get in touch.'

Goodburn, who has undergone significant challenges over the past few years and has tirelessly campaigned for increased awareness of the disease since his cancer diagnoses, remarkably reached the 50m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last week.

Andy Burnham has invited Archie Goodburn to a personal meeting to discuss cancer research

The British Commonwealth Games swimmer broke down on BBC Breakfast as he made a direct and emotional plea to the Prime Minister to improve brain cancer research funding on Tuesday

While appearing on BBC Breakfast on Tuesday, the swimmer stared down the barrel of the camera and broke down in tears as he made a direct plea to Downing Street, saying: 'Andy Burnham, if you believe and want to make a change and a difference to the future of our country and our young population, please listen to us.

'Please establish a national brain cancer lead and give us a chance to fight for our lives because the things that patients are going through out there is unbelievable and so unjust.

'There are clinical trials around the world, in the US, in Australia, in China, that could change lives. We are not seeing them in the UK and it is unfair and unjust.

'Please invest and make the difference. I'm on my knees begging for not just my own life but for those of my best friends and those that are affected and the families around the country.

'This has to change. It's been going for too long and the suffering is unbearable.'

His emotional plea came after the Rare Cancers Bill, aimed at improving research and trials into rare types of the disease, had become law earlier this year.

'It's a step in the right direction but it's not going to make the changes that we need,' he continued. 'I'm extremely grateful for Dr Scott Arthur and the work he's done there.

Goodburn, who was diagnosed inoperable brain tumours at just 22, remarkably reached the 50m breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last week

'The Rare Cancers Bill covers 14 different types of rare cancers. Brain cancer is one of these in terms of incidents of diagnosis, but it's not the same in terms of the number of deaths it causes.

'Yes it's rare, but it's extremely deadly. This frustrates me immensely.

'The rare cancers bill establishes two new positions: a clinical lead and a research lead. These two roles are part-time across 14 different types of cancers and they accumulate to 36 days a year.

'There's two roles to cover 14 different types of cancer and change the landscape of treatment.

'I do not see how 36 days a year is going to make that change for 14 different types of cancers, let alone the most deadly type of cancer.'

Sports.title: Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open
Sports.content:
Jack Draper breaks down in tears as Brit loses on return from injury at Canadian Open

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jack Draper's torturous attempts to return to tennis continued as he wiped away tears during defeat in the first round of the Canadian Open.

Trailing Frenchman Terence Atmane 4-1 in the deciding set, the British former world No4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept.

It was a truly wretched sight and, while we must wait for the man himself to speak, it seems likely those tears were an indication that he is still feeling the pain of an arm injury which simply will not leave him alone.

Some natural ring-rust aside, there was nothing much wrong with Draper’s level in the first two sets, and when he won the second comfortably he looked well placed to take the match. But his serve began to subside dramatically and by the end he could do little more than just roll it over. The 24-year-old also, in apparent desperation, started to hit an increasing number of dropshots.

Atmane, in terrible form himself, won 6-3, 2-6, 6-2.

It has been well over 12 months now that Draper has struggled with bone bruising in the humerus of his left arm.

Jack Draper was in tears during the third set of his game against Terence Atmane in Montreal as he continues his return from injury 🎾 pic.twitter.com/ekhBse3Af3 — Sky Sports Tennis (@SkySportsTennis) August 4, 2026

Jack Draper was reduced to tears as he lost his comeback match following time out with injury

The British former world No 4 sat in his chair at the changeover and wept in the final set

Due to play at Wimbledon, he pulled out the day before his match. Set to return in Washington, he withdrew citing a twinge in that arm.

The injury is clearly chronic and, if this is indeed yet another setback, it is not easy to see where Draper goes from here.

Draper said earlier this week: 'It's important for people to recognise that the injury I have is very complex, it's very complicated and everyone around me is doing everything we can to help this keep moving along.

'It's not as simple as 'rest and heal up and you'll come back and you'll be fine'.

Terribly sad to say, it is becoming increasingly likely we may never see the best of this beautifully, brutally brilliant player again.

Sports.title: British boxer rushed to hospital after suffering bleed on her brain
Sports.content:
British boxer rushed to hospital after suffering bleed on her brain

Raven Chapman, 32, who fought for a world title in 2024, was in Denmark last month when she collapsed and was rushed to hospital

View Image Raven Chapman throws a punch at Kariss Artingstall

British boxer Raven Chapman is in hospital after suffering a bleed on the brain during a sparring session.

‌



Chapman, 32, who fought for a world title in 2024, was training in Denmark last month when she collapsed and was rushed to hospital. A fundraiser has been launched to raise money for her recovery.

‌



A statement from her team read: "On Friday, July 24 , Raven unexpectedly collapsed after a sparring session in Denmark. Emergency services were called immediately, and she was airlifted to a local hospital. She was diagnosed with a brain haematoma and cerebral oedema.

‌



"Raven underwent emergency surgery immediately. The procedure successfully stopped the bleeding and helped stabilise the swelling. She was then placed in a medically induced coma. Over the past day, she has been taken off the sedatives and is continuing to receive treatment while awaiting medically supervised repatriation to a hospital in the UK, where her rehabilitation is expected to take some time.

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury winner offered world title shot READ MORE :

"Her doctors are doing everything they can to support her recovery, and we remain hopeful as she continues to fight through this incredibly difficult time. Raven’s family are in Denmark supporting her during this incredibly difficult time. We kindly ask that their privacy is respected.

Article continues below

"At this stage, this is the only update we are able to provide. If there are any significant developments, we will share further information when it is appropriate to do so. Thank you for your continued support. Please keep Raven and her loved ones in your thoughts during this challenging time."

Chapman turned professional in 2021 and won her first nine fights before losing to world champion Skye Nicolson. Chapman was then beaten in her next fight when she challenged Karriss Artingstall for the British featherweight title. The Norwich fighter bounced back earlier this summer when she stopped Georgia Klein.

Chapman's incident comes after Irish fighter Lee Reeves was taken out of the ring on a stretcher in Dublin last weekend. He remains in hospital while a fundraiser has raised more than €50,000 to cover medical costs and his recovery.

Sports.title: Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal, Newcastle and secret transfer battle both clubs are desperate to win
Sports.content:
There we have it then. Bruno Guimaraes will join Arsenal from Newcastle in a deal worth £75million.

It has become a familiar trend for the Magpies. Stand firm in the face of interest from their Premier League rivals, before ultimately sanctioning an agreement.

Guimaraes follows Alexander Isak and Sandro Tonali out of St James’ Park. A talent drain which has seen ambition move from conquering Europe to being able to qualify for it in the first place.

But as the dust settles on another transfer saga, the real battle begins in earnest. The PR war.

‌



It’s the battle every club is desperate to win. The battle played out in secret, with the victor usually declared on social media.

Arsenal set to agree blockbuster Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Newcastle demands finally met READ MORE :

Winning favour with supporters after signing a player is easy, nobody has ever complained about receiving a shiny new toy. But for the selling club, it’s about softening the blow and explaining why they would have been silly not to do it in the first place.

Guimaraes to Arsenal is perhaps a perfect case study. After all, initial reports suggested Newcastle wanted £100m for their Brazilian talisman.

That’s the amount they received for Tonali, while Isak fetched a British record £125m a year ago. So the final figure is a huge win for the Gunners, whittling down £25m for a player Mikel Arteta was desperate to land.

‌



Arsenal will rightly suggest that in a market that has seen Elliot Anderson and Morgan Rogers go for more than £100m, getting Guimaraes for £75m in 2026 is quite frankly a bit of a bargain (in ridiculous Premier League terms).

Case closed then, Arsenal the winners, Newcastle the losers…cue gloating from the Gunners and meltdown from the Magpies. Or perhaps not so fast.

Because from the Newcastle side, this is unequivocally another transfer win. The Chronicle report that the Gunners opened negotiations with a frankly paltry offer of £45m.

‌



That wouldn’t even get you a Crysencio Summerville in a transfer window which has seemed to only veer from the ludicrous to the ridiculous.

Newcastle needed a bidding war to even get close to their valuation…or so they feared. Sources from Tyneside insist Arsenal were bidding against themselves, such was their desperation to land the midfielder.

In the end, Newcastle will boost their coffers to the tune of £75m, for a player - while still at the peak of his powers - will turn 29 in November.

View 2 Images Newcastle will receive £75m up-front for the Brazilian midfielder (Image: Shaun Botterill - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



And unlike so many modern transfers, it has been stressed this will be paid up-front, immediately giving the Toon a much needed cash-injection. And let’s not beat around the bush, they need that.

They need to change the narrative on a window which has seen key players AND Eddie Howe leave the club. They also need to provide prospective new boss Matthias Jaissle some funds to build the squad in his image - and that doesn't mean just doing what they've done so far, and signing potential. They need high-quality, Premier League ready performers for the here and now.

Arsenal felt they needed Guimaraes. A player that can help them retain their Premier League crown, while going one step further in Europe.

And so, who really won the saga? That will really depend on what you read, the same for every major deal this summer, as clubs scramble to shape the narrative in their direction.

‌



But this could be one of the great rarities in modern football. A transfer that probably suits both teams equally well.

Both sets of fans can shake hands and be on with their day then. That’s probably how it will work on social media…right?

Football icon Cristiano Ronaldo and his wife-to-be, Georgina Rodriguez, live a life of luxury. The couple are reportedly set to tie the knot in the coming days, with Saturday, August 8, rumoured to be the date.

‌



According to The Sun, Ronaldo and Rodriguez will marry on the ex-Manchester United star's home island of Madeira. The forward is believed to have chosen a cathedral in Funchal for the occasion.

‌



A glamorous yet tasteful wedding was perhaps the only outcome for a couple whose relationship has been characterised by luxury ever since they became an item in 2016.

‌



The Portuguese legend met his partner, an Argentinian/Spanish model, in Madrid ten years ago when he was playing for Real Madrid and Rodriguez was working in a Gucci shop

Fast forward to 2026 and the duo have five children together, with three from Ronaldo's previous relationships. They became engaged in August 2025 and the happy couple have flaunted their staggering wealth over the years, giving fans an insight into their opulent lifestyle.

The Al-Nassr star has ensured his bride has a stunning engagement ring too, estimated at around £4.5m. Ahead of their nuptials, Ronaldo is believed to have showered Rodriguez with gifts.

Sports.title: Man Utd break silence on ticket controversy and admit causing 'significant distress'
Sports.content:
Man Utd break silence on ticket controversy and admit causing 'significant distress'

Manchester United have owned the fact their ticket investigation has caused distress to a number of fans, who thought they may lose their season tickets, with the club wanting to clamp down on touting

View 2 Images Man Utd have conceded that they made mistakes with their ticket investigation, which negatively impacted fans (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have admitted causing "distress" to fans by launching an investigation into how season ticket account details are used - leaving long-time and genuine supporters fearing they could lose their tickets.

‌



The Premier League giants began the process last month after they identified a number of accounts which they claim had activity which warranted further investigation.

‌



Red flags were raised when United clocked that, in one instance, 1,088 accounts had been accessed on a single device, according to the club, who have continued to defend their actions in private.

‌



But a host of genuine fans were left fearful that their season tickets would be confiscated without knowing the reasons and in a fans forum on July 30 those emotions were laid bare. United have now accepted they made mistakes in how they chose to execute their investigation.

Man Utd closing in on transfer deal after Michael Carrick dropped hint READ MORE :

The club said in a statement: "Manchester United accepts that the process may have caused distress for some loyal supporters, underestimated how common sharing account usernames and passwords was, and recognises that some fans may have felt they were being treated unfairly,"

"We recognise that many supporters have shared account login details in circumstances they regarded as legitimate, and we did not anticipate the extent to which this was occurring."

‌



United say a "satisfactory explanation" has been provided in a "substantial number of cases" with those individuals seeing any restrictions removed from their accounts.

View 2 Images Man Utd fans have expressed their anger with the treatment of long-term supporters

The club also believe the reasons for their investigation were valid amid a growing touting issue which, they say, deprives supporters of the opportunity to buy tickets. They have also maintained that any season tickets which are confiscated will be repurposed as season tickets - not sold as a corporate hospitality packages.

‌



United added: "There is no doubt at all this process has uncovered significant and organised touting which will enable us to remove tickets from touts and place them back in the hands of genuine fans. We believe this is something we are all aligned on."

The way in which United have treated their season ticket holders has come in for criticism. Last season, the club moved 500 season ticket holders from seats they had used for years in order to accommodate an increase in hospitality tickets.

Sports.title: Ex-jockey Robby Aldorado who died after heart surgery had texted: ‘I feel like a new person’
Sports.content:
Ex-jockey Robby Aldorado who died after heart surgery had texted: ‘I feel like a new person’

One of the most successful riders in US history with more than 5,000 wins, the 52-year-old was best known for his association with the two-time Horse of the Year Curlin

View 3 Images Jockey Robby Albarado: died in his sleep (Image: Getty Images)

Retired jockey Robby Albarado has died after heart surgery just days after texting a trainer, ‘I feel like a new person’.

‌



The 52-year-old was one of the most successful riders in US history with more than 5,000 wins and a hugely successful association with two-time Horse of the Year, Curlin. He won ten races on the Steve Asmussen-trained Curlin, including the Preakness Stakes and Breeders’ Cup Classic in 2007 and the following year’s Dubai World Cup.

‌



Since he retired at the end of 2021 he had been working as an exercise rider for top trainer Kenny McPeek, for whom he steered Swiss Skydiver to victory in the 2020 Preakness.

‌



Visiting jockey from country where whip use is forbidden gets 22-day Goodwood ban READ MORE :

Tony Bloom's Royal Ascot heroine ruled out for rest of season after injury blow READ MORE :

According to McPeek, Alborado underwent surgery on July 30 to have a stent inserted to clear a blockage near his heart.

He had been released from hospital and was staying at McPeek’s home in Saratoga when he was found dead on Tuesday morning, August 4, by the trainer’s wife.

“We had him here at the house, he was just resting, best we can figure he died in his sleep last night between 8pm. and this morning,” Kenny McPeek told DRF.com “Sherri found him upstairs at 11.30am.”

‌



View 3 Images Robby Albarado celebrates after riding Curlin in the Dubai World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

The trainer added: “Not only did we work together, we were close friends. Probably the highest moment was when we won the Preakness with Swiss Skydiver. World-class horseman. Great friend.”

Albarado rode 5,222 career winners, of which 40 were at Grade 1 level, with 1,192 during a five year period at Churchill Downs.

‌



His other big wins included the 2011 Breeders’ Cup Mile on Court Vision for trainer Dale Romans.

View 3 Images Curlin: won the 2008 Dubai World Cup (Image: Getty Images)

Romans, president of the Kentucky Horsemen’s Benevolent and Protective Association told the Paulick Report : “Just devastated by the loss of Robby Albarado. We shared great victories and unforgettable moments, but above all, he was family. Our hearts and prayers are with his children and everyone who loved him.

‌



“He was my main rider for a long time. He was a good friend to his friends, including me. He was hard-working, talented at what he did, was always upbeat, a good man to be around. He texted me Sunday: ‘I feel like a new person,’ with a muscle emoji.

“To pick out one race he rode for me, Court Vision would be the one. He got up by a nose. He told me the week before, working him on the turf, that he’d never been better and he could win this race. And he won the Breeders’ Cup Mile at 60-1. Got up by a whisker.

Albarado was married twice and had five children.

Sports.title: Chad le Clos shares heartbreaking update as fire at home during Commonwealth Games kills neighbour
Sports.content:
Chad le Clos shares heartbreaking update as fire at home during Commonwealth Games kills neighbour

Chad le Clos made history at the Commonwealth Games this summer but back home tragedy struck as his long-term home was burned down in a fire, which killed a resident

View 2 Images Chad le Clos has seen his apartment in South Africa destroyed by a fire

Chad le Clos's apartment in South Africa was destroyed by a fire whilst he was becoming the most successful athlete in Commonwealth Games history last week.

‌



The tragedy took place the night after the swimmer made history in Glasgow. He landed his 21st medal - overtaking Australia's Emma McKeon as the athlete with the most medals in Commonwealths history - when South Africa took bronze in the men's 4x100m medley relay.

‌



It was the 34-year-old's third medal of the 2026 Games, where he also won won silver in the mixed 4x100 ⁠medley and bronze in the men's 4x100 freestyle relays.

‌



But whilst he was making history in Scotland, back home in South Africa a fire destroyed his long-term home in Sea Point, Cape Town and killed one of his neighbours.

He said on Instagram: "It has taken me a while to process this heartbreaking tragedy. On the evening of 30 July, amid breaking the all-time Commonwealth record, a fire started in my apartment block, which quickly spread to my home.

"Sadly my home, where I've lived for more than a decade, burnt down and there is nothing left to salvage. No words can truly ease a loss like this, but I hope the family knows that the thoughts of an entire community are with them.

‌



"It is with a heavy heart that I extend my deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and friends of my neighbour of many years, who tragically lost his life in this fire. No words can truly ease a loss like this, but I hope the family knows that the thoughts of an entire community are with them."

According to local reports a 93-year-old man tragically died.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Le Clos also added: "To my fellow neighbours whose homes and lives have been severely affected by this fire, please know that you are not alone. This is a tight-knit community and it is in moments like these that we lean on one another.

"I also want to express my heartfelt thanks for the overwhelming support shown by family, friends and the broader community. Watching neighbours come together to help one another has been a genuine source of comfort amid the tragedy. "Finally, thank you to the Fire Department, first responders, SAPS and all emergency services personnel who responded so swiftly and worked tirelessly through the night."

View 2 Images The South African opened up about the tragedy on social media

Article continues below

Le Clos shot to prominence when he famously beat Michael Phelps to win 200m butterfly gold at the London Olympics in 2012. Phelps was a 14-time Olympic champion and had not lost in the event since 2001 before he was outgunned.

It led to a now iconic interview, which has stood the test of him, between BBC's Clare Balding and Bert le Clos, Chad's father. Alongside that legendary gold he also picked up the silver in the 100m butterfly. Four years later in Rio de Janeiro he came second in the 200m freestyle and the 100 butterfly.

The South African won his first Commonwealth medal in Delhi in 2010 at the age of 18 and now boasts seven gold, five silver and nine bronze medals having competed at five editions of the Games.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
