World.title: Graham Arnold extends Iraq contract ahead of Gulf Cup and AFC Asian Cup 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq national team head coach Graham Arnold has officially signed a contract extension with the Iraq Football Association (IFA), ensuring he will remain in charge of the Lions of Mesopotamia for the country’s upcoming major international tournaments.

The renewal secures Arnold’s position on the sidelines as Iraq prepares for the Gulf Cup and the 2027 AFC Asian Cup, providing continuity as the national team continues its long-term development.

According to a source within the Iraq Football Association, Arnold finalized the agreement on Wednesday, extending his tenure as head coach of the Iraqi national football team.

The new deal confirms that the Australian manager will oversee Iraq’s preparations and participation in the upcoming Gulf Cup before leading the team into the AFC Asian Cup 2027.

The contract extension reflects the federation’s confidence in Arnold’s leadership and its desire to maintain stability ahead of two of the region’s most important football competitions.

Keeping the same coaching staff allows Iraq to continue building tactical consistency, squad cohesion, and long-term planning without interruption.

The upcoming Gulf Cup will provide valuable competitive experience before the national team shifts its focus to the AFC Asian Cup, where Iraq will aim to compete for continental honors.

Coaching continuity is considered an important factor in international football, particularly as teams prepare for major tournaments.

By extending Arnold’s contract, the Iraq Football Association signals its commitment to maintaining the current technical project while continuing preparations for future regional and Asian competitions.

Further details regarding the duration and financial terms of the renewed agreement have not yet been officially disclosed.

World.title: Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt agree to boost trilateral cooperation
World.content:
Amman (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening trilateral cooperation by activating specialized technical committees and expanding coordination across key economic sectors, including investment, industry, and energy.

The agreement was reached during a trilateral ministerial meeting held in Amman, where the three countries also discussed regional developments, the situation in the Strait of Hormuz, and the importance of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions across the Middle East.

According to a statement from Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein participated in the meeting alongside Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi and Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty.

The meeting took place ahead of the Arab ministerial meeting on Jerusalem and focused on accelerating implementation of the Iraq-Jordan-Egypt cooperation mechanism.

The ministers agreed to activate the partnership through specialized technical committees and hold regular meetings at various levels to monitor the progress of joint initiatives.

The three countries emphasized expanding cooperation in strategic sectors that support long-term economic growth.

Discussions focused on increasing collaboration in:

Economic development

Investment projects

Industrial cooperation

Trade facilitation

Infrastructure development

Officials said stronger coordination would help deepen regional economic integration while creating new opportunities for sustainable growth.

Energy cooperation was a central topic during the talks, with ministers reviewing ongoing and future projects involving:

Oil cooperation

Electricity interconnection

Regional energy security

Cross-border energy infrastructure

The three governments stressed that expanding joint energy initiatives would contribute to improving energy security and strengthening economic ties between Iraq, Jordan, and Egypt.

The ministers also exchanged views on regional developments, particularly the situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz.

They welcomed ongoing efforts aimed at reopening the strategic waterway as quickly as possible, highlighting its importance for regional stability, international trade, and global energy markets.

The meeting concluded with a joint call for an end to military escalation across the region, emphasizing that dialogue and diplomatic engagement remain the most effective means of resolving regional crises.

The ministers reiterated their shared commitment to peaceful solutions and closer regional cooperation in addressing common political and economic challenges.

World.title: Al Qaim Cement Plant expands exports to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Al-Qaim Cement Plant has reached its full designed production capacity of 840,000 tonnes annually, strengthening domestic cement supplies while increasing exports to neighboring Syria, the Ministry of Industry and Minerals announced on Wednesday.

The achievement marks a significant milestone in Iraq’s efforts to boost local industrial production, reduce reliance on imports, and expand the country’s non-oil exports.

According to the ministry, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant is now operating at its full design capacity, producing approximately 70,000 tonnes of sulfate-resistant cement each month.

The output is sufficient to meet demand across Anbar Province and other Iraqi governorates while supporting the government’s strategy to enhance domestic industrial self-sufficiency.

In addition to serving the local market, the plant currently exports around 7,500 tonnes of cement per month to Syria, reflecting growing cross-border trade and regional demand for Iraqi construction materials.

General Company for Iraqi Cement Director General Zuhair Dawood Ahmed said the facility is operated through a partnership with Al-Maysarah Cement Industry Company.

He explained that the plant features a fully modernized production line equipped with advanced machinery and internationally sourced equipment, alongside a modern centralized control system that manages production processes efficiently.

The factory also includes advanced laboratories for testing both raw materials and finished products, ensuring quality standards are maintained throughout the manufacturing process.

To ensure uninterrupted production, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant operates its own 30-megawatt power station, providing stable electricity independent of the national grid.

This dedicated energy supply enables the plant to maintain around-the-clock production, minimizing operational disruptions and supporting consistent output.

Officials said continuous operations are essential to meeting domestic demand while expanding Iraq’s presence in regional cement markets.

The Ministry of Industry said increasing production at state-owned industrial facilities remains a key objective in supporting economic diversification beyond the oil sector.

By achieving full operational capacity and maintaining exports, the Al-Qaim Cement Plant contributes to strengthening Iraq’s manufacturing base, creating greater industrial resilience, and expanding opportunities for Iraqi products in foreign markets.

The ministry added that efforts will continue to increase cement exports while supporting the country’s infrastructure and construction sectors through reliable local production.

World.title: Iraq lawmakers scrutinize Karbala Refinery contracts amid government anti-corruption drive
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi lawmakers have begun reviewing government contracts suspected of containing inflated costs, as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi intensifies efforts to tighten oversight of public spending and prevent corruption before contracts are approved.

The renewed scrutiny comes a day after Al-Zaidi ordered the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to establish a specialized team responsible for conducting pre-contract financial audits within 10 working days. The initiative aims to identify high costs before agreements are finalized, marking a shift from investigating corruption after it occurs to preventing it at the contracting stage.

MP Haider Mohammed Al-Mutairi, a member of the Ishraqat Kanoun bloc, called on the prime minister to review several contracts related to the Karbala Refinery, arguing that some agreements warrant immediate investigation due to their financial burden on the state.

Al-Mutairi urged the formation of a high-level investigative committee to examine a consultancy contract involving 49 advisers, claiming it costs the Iraqi government approximately $52 million annually.

He also highlighted an operational contract for the refinery valued at $180 million per year, which he said amounts to nearly 750 million Iraqi dinars in daily expenditures.

The MP called for greater transparency in reviewing major state contracts, particularly those involving strategic infrastructure projects.

The parliamentary review follows a broader government campaign to strengthen financial oversight across ministries and state institutions.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi directed the Federal Board of Supreme Audit to implement mandatory pre-audit procedures for government contracts, including setting financial thresholds that determine which agreements require advance scrutiny.

According to the prime minister, inflated contract values and weak oversight have long been among the primary channels through which public funds were lost.

He stressed that Iraq’s next phase of anti-corruption efforts should focus on preventing irregularities before contracts are signed rather than relying solely on post-contract investigations.

The government says the new oversight framework is intended to improve transparency, accelerate contract reviews, and safeguard public finances without delaying legitimate development projects.

The initiative forms part of a wider reform agenda aimed at enhancing accountability, improving governance, and restoring confidence in public procurement procedures.

No official findings regarding the Karbala Refinery contracts have been announced, and any investigation would be subject to the legal and auditing procedures established by Iraqi authorities.

World.title: Iraq studies oil pipeline network to Turkey, Syria, Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Oil Ministry is working on diversifying oil export outlets by constructing a pipeline network that will be extended to ports in Turkey, Syria, and Jordan.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Sunday that the government is studying the construction of the Basra-Haditha-Kirkuk-Ceyhan pipeline as a new route, with branches from Haditha to the Syrian port of Baniyas and the Jordanian port of Aqaba.

Fluctuations in the global oil market have a significant impact on Iraq’s revenue. However, the most significant impact is the decline in daily export volumes, which have been severely affected by the ongoing war in the region, according to al-Rikabi.

The current conflict in the region has led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which is a strategically important waterway that transports the majority of Iraq’s oil shipments.

Al-Rikabi explained that the pipeline from southern Iraq to the port of Ceyhan on the Mediterranean will raise oil export volumes via Turkish territory.

The Iraqi official said earlier that the Basra-Haditha oil pipeline needs to be carried out first to transport crude oil to Haditha in the western province of Anbar, and then preparation for the alternate pipeline takes place.

The project’s feasibility study is presently underway, and if completed, the pipeline will serve as an alternative for oil tankers now transporting oil to the Syrian port of Baniyas.

The Iraqi cabinet decided in April to move forward with the implementation of the Basra-Haditha oil pipeline.

According to reports, the project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha.

The pipeline’s capacity is projected to be approximately 2.25 million barrels per day using 56-inch diameter pipes. This design aims to enhance domestic transportation and establish connections to future export facilities.

The pipeline will be 685 kilometers long and will serve as the initial phase in the construction of a pipeline network that might eventually extend to Jordan and Syria.

The state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC) and State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) are building the project, which is funded by the Iraq-China Framework Agreement.

The pipeline provides a direct path to both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and, subsequently, to European markets.

Once completed, the project will improve flexibility, as Iraq studies alternative routes to its present seaports to expand export capacity.

World.title: Iraq in talks with Iran to facilitate vessel transit through Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair said on Tuesday that discussions are taking place with Iran regarding the transit of oil tankers via the Strait of Hormuz, with an anticipated agreement in the near future.

In a statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Khudair stated that the economic and political discussions held during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran addressed approaches to expand cooperation and resulted in signing several agreements.

The Iraqi delegation held talks with Iranian counterparts to ensure the safe transit of vessels across the Strait of Hormuz and protect oil shipments, according to Khudair.

The oil minister stressed that the policy of the Iraqi government is based on building communication channels and partnerships with neighboring countries to support the national economy.

The two parties’ discussions aim to avert future interruptions to Iraqi oil exports amid growing regional maritime concerns.

As Baghdad depends heavily on the Strait of Hormuz, it seeks to secure a deal for the safe passage of oil shipments through the waterway.

While Iran has previously shown a willingness to make exceptions for friendly or non-hostile neighbors, practical implementation and approval processes remain a primary focus of continuing discussions.

World.title: Iraq’s liquidity crisis causes delays in paying public servants
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is experiencing a serious financial and liquidity problem, causing delays in paying state employees.

The fall in income from oil, due to the difficulties of exporting via the Strait of Hormuz, has put the Finance Ministry of Iraq in a deficit by trillions of dinars.

The Iraqi government is considering home loans to finance its enormous monthly salaries.

Crude oil exports, which account for approximately 90 percent of Iraq’s federal income, fell dramatically because of the military operations in the region and maritime shipping difficulties.

Iraq requires between 8 and 11 trillion Iraqi dinars ($6.1 billion to $8.4 billion) every month to pay millions of governmental staff and pensioners.

The country’s income fell significantly below expenditure demands, resulting in a large monthly shortfall and an acute cash crisis.

Payrolls have experienced extraordinary delays, causing public concern and reducing local economic activity.

Financing shortfalls have put a burden on government-owned enterprises, particularly drug delivery in the health sector.

Authorities aim to engage in temporary local borrowing to avoid incurring further international debt, as well as long-term calls for diversified state resources.

World.title: Dana Gas, Crescent Petroleum supply Baghdad with gas for electricity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Dana Gas and Crescent Petroleum said on Tuesday that they started supplying the electricity ministry with natural gas from the Khor Mor field in Iraqi Kurdistan under an agreement to support the country’s electricity output.

An agreement was reached last December between the Electricity Ministry and the two companies to supply 100 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the Khor Mor facility to the Taza gas-fired power plant in Kirkuk province for a period of one year.

The step took place after a project to increase the production capacity of the Khor Mor gas field to 750 million cubic feet per day was completed.

The completion of the expansion project increased the availability of additional gas quantities to local markets through the pipeline network, as reported by Shafaq News.

Majid Jafar, CEO of Crescent Petroleum and Managing Director of Dana Gas, stated that the gas transfer to the Electricity Ministry in Baghdad marks an important milestone in Iraqi Kurdistan’s gas sector growth.

Jafar explained that this development will address the growing demand for electricity and enhance the services offered to residents.

Richard Hall, CEO of Dana Gas Group, described the deal as an important step reflecting the outcomes of the production growth program.

According to Hall, the agreement paves the way for enhanced collaboration within Iraq’s energy sector, strengthens energy security, and contributes to the stability of the electricity grid.

The Khor Mor gas project provides the fuel required to produce more than 80 percent of the energy in Iraqi Kurdistan, which supplies power to over eight million people.

World.title: Jharkhand recruitment protests: CM Hemant Soren says 'action soon'; CJP extends support - top developments
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand chief minister Hemant Soren on Wednesday said his government would "soon take action" over the ongoing protests against alleged irregularities in state recruitment examinations after meeting Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar.

"I met the Governor today and discussed the situation; it is being looked into, we will soon take action," Soren told reporters.

Students demand cancellation of JPSC exam, CBI probe

The protests began after the results of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination were declared on July 5, with aspirants alleging irregularities in the recruitment process. Students have since been holding round-the-clock demonstrations and an indefinite sit-in, demanding transparency, accountability and reforms in the state's recruitment agencies.

The protesters are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination, a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC-CGL recruitment examinations, and the public release of OMR sheets and answer scripts. A section of the protesters has warned of gheraoing the Jharkhand Assembly on August 6 if their demands are not addressed.

Hunger strike continues; student leader ends water boycott

Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC), consumed water on Wednesday, the fourth day of his fast.





Mahto said he decided to drink water after climate activist Sonam Wangchuk appealed to him to do so during a video call. However, he said the hunger strike and the ongoing satyagraha would continue until the government addressed the students' demands.

The state's Criminal Investigation Department (CID), which is probing the alleged examination irregularities, has conducted raids at multiple locations across Jharkhand.

Officials have seized laptops, mobile phones, bank documents, carbon copies of OMR sheets and other materials, which are being examined as part of the investigation.

World.title: Beyond Donations: How CSR Is Rewriting India’s Education Story
World.content:
For years, corporate social responsibility (CSR) in education was measured by the number of classrooms built, computers donated, or scholarships awarded. Today, that metric is changing.

As Indiaâs education system moves beyond expanding access towards improving learning outcomes, companies are increasingly investing in programmes that strengthen govt schools, train teachers, improve employability and build long-term partnerships with public institutions.

The shift comes at a critical moment. India has largely succeeded in getting children into school. According to UDISE+ 2024-25, the country has 14.7 lakh schools, 24.7 crore students, and 1 crore teachers.

Rural enrolment among children aged 6-14 has reached 98%, while literacy among those aged seven and above stands at 81%.

But the next challenge is ensuring children actually learn. The Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) 2024 shows that among Class III students in govt schools, the proportion able to read a Class II-level text improved from 16.3% in 2022 to 23.4% in 2024, while those able to solve subtraction rose from 20.2% to 27.6%.





The gains are encouraging but also underline the distance still to be covered.

Govt initiatives such as NIPUN Bharat, Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI and DIKSHA are attempting to address this challenge through foundational literacy, teacher training, digital learning and school infrastructure. Yet the scale of the task means govts alone cannot do everything. That is where CSR is beginning to play a more strategic role.

Education has emerged as the single largest recipient of CSR funding in India. According to the latest CSRBOX report, India Inc spent Rs 40,794 crore on CSR during FY2024-25 across more than 72,000 projects. Education accounted for Rs 13,877 crore, or 34% of the total, making it the countryâs biggest CSR sector. More significantly, companies are moving away from one-off philanthropy towards multi-year programmes, govt partnerships and data-driven monitoring of outcomes.

Bharti Airtel Foundation offers one example of this transition. During FY2024-25, the foundation reported reaching more than 22 lakh students across over 16,000 schools. Its cumulative programmes have impacted 3.7 million students, more than 36,000 schools, and over 3.3 lakh teachers.

Rather than focusing solely on infrastructure, its initiatives include teacher support, school transformation, life skills, and community engagement.

Its Satya Bharti School Programme operates 164 rural schools across four states, while its Quality Support Programme works with govt schools in 12 states.

Another example is Tata STRIVE, which reflects the growing emphasis on employability. In FY2024-25, it directly reached over 4.5 lakh young people and reported cumulative outreach of more than 22.5 lakh beneficiaries through skill development, career guidance, vocational education and entrepreneurship programmes.

The focus extends beyond classrooms to ensuring education translates into livelihoods and economic participation.

This evolution mirrors the changing needs of Indiaâs education system. While access has improved dramatically, important gaps remain. Nearly 8% of 15-16-year-olds are no longer enrolled in school, with girls recording slightly higher non-enrolment than boys.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Infrastructure has also improved unevenly. Although over 99% of schools have drinking water and nearly 94% have electricity, only about two-thirds have computers and internet access, while just 35.6% have dedicated toilets for children with special needs.

These are challenges that require sustained investment rather than isolated interventions. Increasingly, CSR is being used not to substitute public spending but to complement it by piloting new models, supporting teachers, strengthening school systems and helping govts scale successful practices.

India has already built one of the worldâs largest education systems. The next phase is about making that scale deliver better outcomes. Public investment will remain the foundation, but if current trends continue, CSR could become an important catalyst in helping schools move from expanding access to improving learning, ensuring that every rupee invested delivers lasting change for students, teachers and communities.

World.title: Cabinet secretary TV Somanathan, home secretary Govind Mohan get one-year extensions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The government on Wednesday granted one-year extensions to cabinet secretary TV Somanathan and home secretary Govind Mohan, ahead of the completion of their original two-year tenures later this month.

The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet extended Mohan's tenure till August 23, 2027, and Somanathan's till August 30, 2027, or until further orders, whichever is earlier in both cases.

Mohan is a 1989-batch IAS officer of the Sikkim cadre. He took charge as home secretary on August 23, 2024, succeeding Ajay Kumar Bhalla, who is now serving as the governor of Manipur.

Somanathan, a 1987-batch IAS officer of the Tamil Nadu cadre, has been serving as cabinet secretary since August 30, 2024. He succeeded Raji Gauba, the longest-serving cabinet secretary who held the post for five years.

World.title: Delhi High Court declines PIL seeking review of Parliament security
World.content:
The Delhi High Court on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) declined to entertain a public interest litigation seeking a review of the safety and security of Parliament, observing that such matters fall within the domain of the executive and Parliament itself.

A Bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia said the Court could not issue directions on how Parliament should manage its administrative or operational affairs.

“These are not the functions of the court. How can any such direction be issued with respect to the functioning of Parliament? You think the Parliament of this country is incapable of taking care of its own security? What kind of a petition is this? We are there to give directions to Parliament as to how their administrative and operational mechanisms should function?” the Bench told the petitioner’s counsel.

The petition, filed by one Raj Singh, referred to the 2001 terrorist attack on Parliament and the 2023 security breach to argue that the existing security framework required a fresh review.

The petitioner’s counsel emphasised that in a parliamentary democracy, the “Parliament is paramount” and reviewing its safety was the “need of the hour”.

“Stampede occurring in a railway station, you don’t see. Security concerns being faced by pedestrians, you don’t see. Security concerns being faced by morning walkers, you don’t see. Security of daily passengers going to railway stations is not a concern?” the Court remarked.

The plea said the issue of reviewing Parliament’s security assumed greater significance due to the increasing frequency of demonstrations directed towards lawmakers.

“Calls for citizens to assemble or march towards Parliament (Sansad Chalo) have become a recurring feature of democratic mobilisation across a range of public issues. While peaceful assembly and freedom of expression remain constitutionally protected, such developments also underline the necessity of ensuring that the existing security framework remains capable of simultaneously safeguarding democratic participation and protecting the institutional integrity and uninterrupted functioning of Parliament,” the petition said.

It therefore sought a direction to the Centre, as well as the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats, to “undertake a comprehensive review of the existing institutional framework governing the safety, security, resilience and uninterrupted constitutional functioning of the Parliament of India, including its administrative, institutional, operational, technological and cyber-security mechanisms, in light of evolving security challenges and emerging threats.”

World.title: Tamil Nadu Budget: Palaniswami gives ‘zero marks’ to TVK government’s first Budget
World.content:
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) criticised the first Budget presented by the TVK-led coalition government, saying he would give it only “zero marks.”

Speaking to reporters at the Secretariat after the presentation of the Budget, Mr. Palaniswami said the ruling party had made several promises before coming to power, but none of them had found a place in the Budget. He alleged that the government had merely renamed existing schemes.

“The TVK had made several poll promises before coming to power. But there is not a single new scheme in the Budget. Only a sticker has been pasted on the existing schemes. None of the poll promises were fulfilled,” he said.

He recalled that the TVK had promised to increase the monthly entitlement for women to ₹2,500, and the old-age pension to ₹3,000. However, no announcement was made in this regard in the Budget, he said. “What happened to the promise of increasing the medical insurance cover to ₹25 lakh for all families,” he asked.

Mr. Palaniswami said the government had not taken any concrete steps to address the revenue deficit. “There are no proper commitments to restore the State’s financial position. Merely forming a committee will not restore the State finances,” Mr. Palaniswami said, adding that even the previous DMK government had formed an expert committee, but ended up increasing the debt by ₹5 lakh crore.

Referring to the AIADMK regime, he said the party had implemented schemes such as the gold-for-thaali scheme and distribution of goats and cows.

World.title: Meta CEO apologises for CSAM, deepfake content; errors in operating platform, say sources
World.content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has apologised for child abuse content, deepfakes and errors in operating the platform, sources said on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) after the company's global team met IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, following the government's recent summons over the removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's post on Facebook.

Government sources said it was made clear to the Meta team that they are not covered under the 'intermediary' definition.

The social media platform selects who receives the content, and Safe harbour under the IT Act is not applicable, according to sources.

Meta team admitted that a lot of money was paid for boosting a certain type of content; they apologised and regretted the mistake, they added.

Meta team, including Global Affairs officer Joel Kaplan, on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) met IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw and had a separate meeting with IT Secretary S. Krishnan.

The meeting assumes significance as the government had summoned Meta's top global executives after Prime Minister Modi's recent Facebook post addressing Indian youth and promising stringent action against paper leaks was briefly restricted on the platform.

While the U.S.-headquartered social media giant had attributed the incident to a technical glitch and apologised, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) had found the explanation "inadequate". The company, which owns Facebook, had said that the content was removed "in error" and was subsequently restored on the platform.

Meta has also been under regulatory scrutiny over the issue of Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM) in paid s on Instagram, and the government, last month, slapped a notice on the social media giant over the issue.

"There are a range of issues... the CSAM issue was raised, so what measures have been taken regarding that, and synthetically generated information ... to what extent that is being looked at. Then, for prominent personalities when they have verified accounts, if content has to be taken down, there have to be safeguards...all of these will be the issues (taken up)," Mr. Krishnan told reporters on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).

Meta, as one of the leading technology companies in the world, should have the technology to address such issues effectively, he had said.

"We would like to understand from them (Meta) as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work, and what are the challenges," Mr. Krishnan added.

For platforms, there needs to be a clear understanding of India's law, what compliance must look like, "and a clearer understanding of how they intend to make sure compliance happens", Mr. Krishnan said.

Government sources had earlier said that the issue is not just about technical aspects, but about "national security and public order". As the government delivers an ultimatum to Meta, the company’s global team will be "categorically" asked to clarify issues around algorithmic bias, how their algorithm operates and the company's role in public order.

In the immediate aftermath of the issue, Meta had informed the IT Ministry that posts by the prime minister and select prominent accounts will be subject to additional oversight on the platform, with multiple levels of checks involving senior company officials. Meta wrote to the government outlining the specifics of enhanced and rigorous safeguards it implemented (on July 28) for content posted by PM Modi and other prominent accounts.

Mr. Modi's July 23 Instagram post, later shared on Facebook, marked his first direct selfie video aimed at engaging with the youth and underscoring the government's commitment to crack down on paper leaks amid students' protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party at that time. The Facebook version of the post was briefly restricted by Meta before being restored.

The IT Ministry maintained that Meta's explanation to the government, citing a technical glitch in the automated content filters, was "not reasonable". They had said that if indeed a glitch in the automated system caused the error, then Meta, being a technology company, must surely hasten to improve its own tools.

Meta officials had attributed the error to AI-powered automated content filters reviewing shared posts and subsequent videos that had circulated following the original post by the prime minister. Meta had told the government that its automated filters inadvertently ended up briefly removing the original post itself.

By summoning global executives, the government wants to ensure that Meta's leadership — all the way to the top — is made fully aware of concerns being raised by Indian authorities. The summoning of global executives, rather than only local representatives, underscores the Centre's intent to directly engage Meta's international leadership on platform accountability.

A Parliamentary standing committee on Wednesday (August 5, 2026) demanded an apology from Meta chief Mark Zuckerberg over Mr. Modi's speech being removed from Facebook.

In a letter to the secretary, Ministry of Electronics and IT, a director of the Lok Sabha secretariat said protection and immunity for Mr. Zuckerberg may be withdrawn if there is no apology in three days.

World.title: Budget evokes mixed reaction
World.content:
The State Budget has evoked a mixed response from different sections of society, with some hailing the document as transformational, while others express their trepidation over the revenue generation aspect.

A Budget for economic growth

The State Budget is an ‘Aspirational, Inspirational and Transformational’ document with significant allocations for major infrastructure projects, operations and maintenance, and capacity building initiatives, according to S.Vaidhyasubramaniam, Vice-Chancellor, SASTRA Deemed University, Thanjavur.

It was an aspirational budget for the youth through education and skilling initiatives, an inspirational budget for the common man to improve quality of living and a transformational budget for the State’s economic growth through ‘Vetri Tamizhagam’ vision document, Mr.Vaidhyasubramanian said in an official release.

Budget lacks income generation avenues – Tax Consultants Federation.

The Thanjavur Tax Consultants Federation has claimed that the Budget lacked income generation avenues and did not guarantee new employment opportunities. Instead, it indicates borrowing of fresh loans for implementing schemes such as ‘Thaimaman Thanga Mothiram’ scheme and others, according to the Federation president, Ravichandran.

World.title: Madhavi Latha highlights factors behind successful  Chenab Bridge construction
World.content:
Scientific excellence, innovation, perseverance, teamwork and meticulous planning helped engineers overcome extraordinary technical challenges to construct the Chenab Railway Bridge in Jammu and Kashmir, one of the world’s most difficult terrains, said G. Madhavi Latha, Professor, Department of Civil Engineering, Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, on Wednesday (August 5, 2026).

Presenting the 83rd Foundation Day Lecture at CSIR-Indian Institute of Chemical Technology (IICT) in Hyderabad, Ms. Madhavi Latha spoke on the construction of the world’s highest railway arch bridge and highlighted the dedication behind the landmark engineering feat. She worked as a geotechnical consultant for it.

The Professor urged young researchers and scientists to pursue their work with passion and commitment. “Work with passion without expectations and never be afraid of failure. Failures and setbacks are an integral part of scientific discovery,” she said. Emphasising the role of technological innovation in research, she said scientists should strive for excellence with resilience, integrity and a long-term vision rather than seeking immediate recognition.

CSIR-IICT Director D. Srinivas Reddy expressed deep admiration for Ms. Madhavi Latha’s contribution to one of India’s most challenging engineering projects. Having personally experienced the difficult terrain and harsh climatic conditions of J&K, he noted that her achievements reflected exceptional determination and engineering expertise.

Mr. Reddy said CSIR-IICT continues to remain at the forefront of research in chemical sciences, pharmaceuticals, catalysis, biotechnology, process engineering, materials science, environmental technologies and sustainable manufacturing, according to a press release.
